title: Countries occupied longest during WWII
prompt: Name the countries that spent the longest continuous period under Axis occupation during World War II.

source.name: Wikipedia — German-occupied Europe / Japanese-occupied territories

disclaimer: Measures continuous occupation duration by any Axis power. Some countries counted from Japanese invasion in 1937 predating the European war. Ranges use commonly cited liberation dates.
trivia: Manchuria was under Japanese control as the puppet state of Manchukuo from 1931 — nearly 14 years, longer than any European occupation. The Channel Islands (UK) were the only British territory occupied by Germany, from June 1940 to May 1945.

title: Most Nobel Prize in Literature laureates
prompt: Name the countries with the most Nobel Prize in Literature laureates by country of citizenship.

source.name: Nobel Foundation — Literature laureates

disclaimer: Counts laureates by country of primary citizenship at time of award. Dual-citizenship laureates may be counted for one country per Nobel Foundation convention.
trivia: France leads with laureates including Sartre (who declined the prize in 1964), Camus, Gide, and most recently Annie Ernaux in 2022.

title: Most Booker Prize winners by nationality
prompt: Name the countries with the most Booker Prize for Fiction winners by author nationality.

source.name: The Booker Prizes — winners archive

disclaimer: Counts each winning author by their primary nationality. The prize opened to all English-language writers in 2014; prior to that only Commonwealth, Irish, and Zimbabwean authors were eligible.
trivia: The UK dominates with dozens of wins including Hilary Mantel (two-time winner for the Wolf Hall trilogy) and Salman Rushdie's Midnight's Children, which was later voted the 'Booker of Bookers'.

title: Most translated authors by origin country
prompt: Name the countries whose authors are most translated worldwide per the UNESCO Index Translationum.

source.name: UNESCO Index Translationum — cumulative statistics

disclaimer: Ranks countries by cumulative count of translated works whose original author is from that country. Reflects works translated into all languages tracked by UNESCO member state national libraries.
trivia: Agatha Christie, Jules Verne, and William Shakespeare are among the individual most-translated authors of all time, boosting the UK, France, and USA totals.

title: Countries where English is an official language
prompt: Name the countries with the largest populations where English is a de jure official (or co-official) language.

source.name: UN member state constitutions / CIA World Factbook

disclaimer: Ranked by total population. Includes countries where English is a co-official language alongside others (e.g. Pakistan, Philippines). Excludes countries where English is merely widely spoken but not official (e.g. USA has no de jure official language federally).
trivia: Despite being the world's largest English-speaking country by fluent speakers, the United States has no federally designated official language and is excluded from this list.

title: Countries where French is an official language
prompt: Name the countries with the largest populations where French is a de jure official (or co-official) language.

source.name: Organisation internationale de la Francophonie — member states

disclaimer: Ranked by total population. Includes countries where French is co-official with local languages (common across West and Central Africa). Excludes observer or associate OIF members without official-language status.
trivia: DR Congo is the world's largest French-speaking country by population, with more French speakers than France itself.

title: Countries where Spanish is an official language
prompt: Name the countries with the largest populations where Spanish is a de jure official (or co-official) language.

source.name: Instituto Cervantes — El español en el mundo

disclaimer: Ranked by total population. Includes only countries where Spanish is de jure official. Excludes the USA (Spanish widely spoken but not federally official) and Belize (English official).
trivia: Mexico has more Spanish speakers than Spain, Argentina, and Colombia combined, and is the largest Spanish-speaking country in the world.

title: Countries where Portuguese is an official language
prompt: Name the countries with the largest populations where Portuguese is a de jure official (or co-official) language.

source.name: Comunidade dos Países de Língua Portuguesa (CPLP)

disclaimer: Ranked by total population. Includes all CPLP member states with Portuguese as an official language. Equatorial Guinea (Portuguese co-official since 2010) is included despite low actual usage.
trivia: Brazil has more Portuguese speakers than the rest of the Lusophone world combined, and its variant of Portuguese is now the most spoken form of the language globally.

title: Countries where Arabic is an official language
prompt: Name the countries with the largest populations where Arabic is a de jure official (or co-official) language.

source.name: Arab League member states / CIA World Factbook

disclaimer: Ranked by total population. Includes all 22 Arab League states plus Chad, Eritrea, and Comoros where Arabic is co-official. Modern Standard Arabic status varies from primary official language to co-official.
trivia: Egypt is the most populous Arabic-speaking country and the cultural heart of the Arab world, producing the largest share of Arabic-language films, music, and television.

title: Most Confucius Institute branches
prompt: Name the countries hosting the most Confucius Institute branches (Chinese government-affiliated language and culture centers).

source.name: Center for Language Education and Cooperation (Hanban)

disclaimer: Counts Confucius Institutes hosted at partner universities. Excludes Confucius Classrooms hosted at primary/secondary schools. Numbers have declined in some Western countries since 2019 due to closures.
trivia: The United States once hosted over 100 Confucius Institutes but the total has declined sharply since 2019 amid concerns over academic freedom, with many US universities closing their branches.

title: Most Goethe-Institut centers
prompt: Name the countries hosting the most Goethe-Institut centers (Germany's official cultural and language institutes abroad).

source.name: Goethe-Institut — worldwide network

disclaimer: Counts full Goethe-Institut branches abroad. Excludes Germany itself (12 centers domestic), reading rooms, and language learning partners. Multiple centers exist in large countries like the USA and India.
trivia: The Goethe-Institut operates in over 90 countries and is Germany's primary soft-power instrument, promoting German language education and cultural exchange since its founding in 1951.

title: Largest goods importers
prompt: Name the countries that import the most merchandise (goods) by total value in USD.

source.name: WTO — World Trade Statistical Review / Trade Statistics

disclaimer: Merchandise (goods) imports only, in current USD. Services trade excluded. EU member states counted separately, not as a bloc.
trivia: The United States has run the world's largest goods import bill nearly every year since 1976, when it overtook West Germany.

title: Largest services exporters
prompt: Name the countries that export the most commercial services by total value in USD.

source.name: WTO — Services trade statistics

disclaimer: Commercial services exports (travel, transport, financial, IT, IP charges, etc.) in current USD. Excludes government services.
trivia: India climbed into the top 5 largely on IT and business-process outsourcing exports, which alone crossed $200B in 2023.

title: Largest services importers
prompt: Name the countries that import the most commercial services by total value in USD.

source.name: WTO — Services trade statistics

disclaimer: Commercial services imports (travel, transport, financial, IT, IP charges, etc.) in current USD. Excludes government services.
trivia: Ireland's services import bill is inflated by multinationals routing intellectual-property royalty payments through Irish subsidiaries.

title: Highest FDI inflows (annual)
prompt: Name the countries that attracted the most foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows in a recent year.

source.name: UNCTAD — World Investment Report

disclaimer: Annual FDI inflows (net) in current USD. Includes equity, reinvested earnings, and intra-company debt. Values swing year to year; ranked by 2023 report.
trivia: Luxembourg and the Netherlands regularly appear because multinationals route capital through their favorable holding-company regimes, not because of real productive investment.

title: Largest inward FDI stock
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total accumulated stock of foreign direct investment held inside their borders.

source.name: UNCTAD — World Investment Report / FDI stocks database

disclaimer: Cumulative inward FDI stock in current USD. Small conduit economies (BVI, Cayman) excluded — only sovereign countries in the answer set.
trivia: The Netherlands hosts the world's largest inward FDI stock per capita, mostly attributable to Special Financial Institutions used by multinationals.

title: Largest current account surpluses
prompt: Name the countries with the largest current account surpluses by USD value.

source.name: IMF — World Economic Outlook / Balance of Payments Statistics

disclaimer: Absolute USD current account surplus (goods + services + primary income + secondary income). Ranks countries in surplus only; deficit countries excluded.
trivia: Germany's current account surplus has been criticized by the IMF and European Commission as excessive relative to its share of eurozone GDP.

title: Largest current account deficits
prompt: Name the countries with the largest current account deficits by USD value.

source.name: IMF — World Economic Outlook / Balance of Payments Statistics

disclaimer: Absolute USD current account deficit. Ranked from largest deficit (most negative) to smallest. Surplus countries excluded.
trivia: The US has run a current account deficit every year since 1982, but as a share of GDP it has narrowed from a 2006 peak near 6% to under 3.5%.

title: Highest sovereign credit rating (AAA)
prompt: Name the countries that hold the top AAA sovereign credit rating from Standard & Poor's.

source.name: S&P Global Ratings — Sovereign Ratings List

disclaimer: S&P long-term foreign-currency sovereign ratings at AAA. There are 11 sovereigns rated AAA — seededDepth reflects the total pool. Ranks tied alphabetically.
trivia: The United States was downgraded from AAA by S&P in 2011 after the debt-ceiling standoff and has not been restored since — Fitch also cut the US to AA+ in 2023.

title: Highest economic complexity
prompt: Name the countries with the highest Economic Complexity Index (ECI) — a measure of the diversity and sophistication of exports.

source.name: Harvard Growth Lab — Atlas of Economic Complexity

disclaimer: Economic Complexity Index (ECI) measures export sophistication and diversity. Higher = more complex. Petro-states and single-commodity exporters score low regardless of GDP.
trivia: Japan has led the ECI rankings every year since the index was created in the 1960s — driven by dominance in precision machinery, electronics and chemicals.

title: Largest US trading partners
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total two-way goods trade with the United States.

source.name: US Census Bureau — Foreign Trade / USTR

disclaimer: Two-way merchandise trade in USD (US exports to + US imports from). Excludes services. The US itself is obviously excluded as an answer.
trivia: Mexico overtook China as the largest US trading partner in 2023 for the first time in over 20 years, driven by nearshoring and higher US tariffs on Chinese goods.

title: Busiest Single Airport (Passengers)
prompt: Name the countries whose busiest single airport handles the most passengers per year.

source.name: Airports Council International (ACI) — World Airport Traffic Rankings

disclaimer: Ranks each country by its single busiest airport's total passenger throughput, not the country's total air traffic. Domestic and international passengers combined.
trivia: Atlanta (ATL) has led the world in passenger traffic almost every year since 1998, and Dubai (DXB) has been the busiest international-only airport for over a decade.

title: Deadliest Roads (Fatality Rate)
prompt: Name the countries with the highest road-traffic fatality rate per 100,000 population.

source.name: WHO — Global Status Report on Road Safety
source.asOf: 2023 WHO Global Status Report (2021 reference year)

disclaimer: Estimated deaths per 100,000 population from road traffic injuries. WHO estimates, which may differ from national police-reported figures.
trivia: Africa has the highest regional road-death rate despite having the fewest vehicles per capita, driven by pedestrian and motorcycle fatalities on mixed-use roads.
asOfDate: 2023 WHO Global Status Report (2021 reference year)

title: Highest EV Market Share (New Cars)
prompt: Name the countries where electric vehicles account for the highest share of new car sales.

source.name: IEA — Global EV Outlook
source.asOf: 2023 new-car sales share, IEA Global EV Outlook 2024

disclaimer: Share of new light-duty car sales that are plug-in electric (BEV + PHEV combined). Nordic markets have led this metric for over a decade.
trivia: Norway crossed 90% EV share in 2024, aided by decades of purchase-tax exemptions, toll discounts, and free public parking that made EVs cheaper to own than combustion cars.
asOfDate: 2023 new-car sales share, IEA Global EV Outlook 2024

title: Most Electric Cars on the Road
prompt: Name the countries with the largest electric-car fleets (cumulative stock of BEV + PHEV passenger vehicles).

source.name: IEA — Global EV Outlook
source.asOf: End-2023 cumulative EV stock, IEA Global EV Outlook 2024

disclaimer: Cumulative on-road stock of battery-electric and plug-in hybrid passenger cars. Different from annual sales — this counts every EV still in service.
trivia: China alone accounts for roughly 60% of the global EV fleet, more than the US, Europe, and the rest of the world combined.
asOfDate: End-2023 cumulative EV stock, IEA Global EV Outlook 2024

title: Longest Expressway Network
prompt: Name the countries with the most kilometres of expressway or motorway (limited-access, grade-separated highway).

source.name: International Road Federation (IRF) — World Road Statistics / national transport ministries

disclaimer: Counts limited-access, grade-separated highways only — not all paved roads or trunk routes. Definitions differ slightly by country (Autobahn, Interstate, motorway, autopista, expressway).
trivia: China built more expressway in the 2010s than the United States built in the entire Interstate era, going from under 20,000 km in 2000 to over 170,000 km today.

title: Largest Rail Passenger Volume
prompt: Name the countries whose railways move the most passenger-kilometres per year.

source.name: International Union of Railways (UIC) — Railway Statistics Synopsis

disclaimer: Measured in passenger-kilometres (one passenger travelling one km). Reflects both ridership and average trip length — commuter-heavy systems and long-distance networks both score high.
trivia: Indian Railways carries more than 8 billion passenger journeys a year — more than any other rail system — but China's high-speed network has now overtaken India in total passenger-km.

title: Largest Rail Freight Volume
prompt: Name the countries whose railways move the most freight (tonne-kilometres) per year.

source.name: International Union of Railways (UIC) — Railway Statistics Synopsis

disclaimer: Measured in tonne-kilometres (one tonne of cargo moved one km). Long-distance bulk-freight countries dominate — passenger-heavy networks rank far lower.
trivia: Freight moves more tonne-km on US rails than on all US highways combined, and coal is still the single largest commodity by weight.

title: Highest Gasoline Prices
prompt: Name the countries where petrol (gasoline) costs the most per litre at the pump.

source.name: GlobalPetrolPrices.com — Gasoline Prices

disclaimer: Retail pump price in US dollars per litre, converted at prevailing exchange rates. Prices reflect a mix of crude cost, refining, distribution, and — usually the biggest single factor — national fuel taxes.
trivia: Hong Kong's petrol is priced high partly because of a HK$6.06/L duty stacked on top of already-tight land prices for filling stations, some of the most expensive real estate in the world.

title: Cheapest Gasoline
prompt: Name the countries where petrol (gasoline) costs the least per litre at the pump.

source.name: GlobalPetrolPrices.com — Gasoline Prices

disclaimer: Retail pump price in US dollars per litre. The cheapest markets are almost all major oil producers that heavily subsidise domestic fuel; prices can shift sharply when subsidies are cut.
trivia: Venezuela's petrol was effectively free for decades thanks to state subsidies — a full tank cost less than a chocolate bar — until the 2020 dual-pricing reform introduced a partly market-rate tier.

title: Highest Public Transport Use
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of daily commuting trips taken by public transport (bus, metro, rail, tram).

source.name: UITP — Mobility in Cities Database / national travel surveys

disclaimer: National-level public-transport mode share for commuting and daily travel, aggregated from urban travel surveys. Small city-states and dense East Asian economies dominate; car-dependent countries rank far lower.
trivia: Hong Kong's MTR is one of the only major metros in the world that operates at a profit — largely because it also owns and develops the property above many of its stations.

title: Largest cassava producers
prompt: Name the world's largest cassava-producing countries by volume.

source.name: FAOSTAT — Crops and livestock products

disclaimer: Cassava (manioc/yuca) production in metric tonnes, fresh weight. A tropical root crop, so temperate countries do not appear.
trivia: Nigeria has been the world's top cassava producer for decades, but yields per hectare are typically higher in Southeast Asia where much of the crop is exported as starch and animal feed.

title: Largest sweet potato producers
prompt: Name the world's largest sweet potato-producing countries by volume.

source.name: FAOSTAT — Crops and livestock products

disclaimer: Sweet potato production in metric tonnes. Distinct from yams (which are a different botanical genus).
trivia: China alone typically accounts for more than half of world sweet potato production, though per-capita consumption is higher in parts of sub-Saharan Africa and Papua New Guinea.

title: Largest yam producers
prompt: Name the world's largest yam-producing countries by volume.

source.name: FAOSTAT — Crops and livestock products

disclaimer: True yams (Dioscorea) in metric tonnes — not sweet potatoes, which are sometimes called 'yams' in North America. Production is heavily concentrated in West Africa's 'yam belt'.
trivia: West Africa produces over 95% of the world's yams, and Nigeria alone typically accounts for more than 65% of global output.

title: Largest sugar beet producers
prompt: Name the world's largest sugar beet-producing countries by volume.

source.name: FAOSTAT — Crops and livestock products

disclaimer: Sugar beet production in metric tonnes. Unlike sugar cane, sugar beet grows in temperate climates and dominates European sugar output.
trivia: Sugar beet provides roughly 20% of the world's sugar; the rest comes from sugarcane. Europe historically pioneered beet sugar during Napoleon's cane blockade in the early 1800s.

title: Largest peanut (groundnut) producers
prompt: Name the world's largest peanut (groundnut) producing countries by volume.

source.name: FAOSTAT — Crops and livestock products

disclaimer: Peanuts (groundnuts) in-shell, metric tonnes. Peanuts are legumes, not tree nuts, though they are often grouped with tree nuts in trade data.
trivia: China and India together produce more than half of the world's peanuts, but the United States dominates the international peanut butter trade because most Asian production is consumed as oil or eaten domestically.

title: Largest almond producers
prompt: Name the world's largest almond-producing countries by volume.

source.name: FAOSTAT — Crops and livestock products

disclaimer: Almonds in-shell, metric tonnes. The United States (specifically California) produces the overwhelming majority of the world's almonds.
trivia: Roughly 80% of the world's almonds come from a single US state — California's Central Valley — where the crop depends on the largest managed pollination event on Earth every February.

title: Largest coconut producers
prompt: Name the world's largest coconut-producing countries by volume.

source.name: FAOSTAT — Crops and livestock products

disclaimer: Coconuts in-shell, metric tonnes. Coconut palms require a tropical coastal climate, so production is concentrated in Southeast Asia, South Asia, and the Pacific.
trivia: Indonesia, the Philippines and India together produce roughly three-quarters of the world's coconuts. Coconut oil was the world's leading vegetable oil until the mid-20th century when palm oil overtook it.

title: Largest avocado producers
prompt: Name the world's largest avocado-producing countries by volume.

source.name: FAOSTAT — Crops and livestock products

disclaimer: Avocado production in metric tonnes. Global output has more than doubled since 2010 as export demand from North America and Europe has surged.
trivia: The Michoacán region of Mexico is the only place on Earth certified to export Hass avocados to the United States year-round, and Mexico produces roughly a third of the world's total.

title: Largest mango producers
prompt: Name the world's largest mango-producing countries by volume (includes mangosteens and guavas as grouped by FAO).

source.name: FAOSTAT — Crops and livestock products

disclaimer: FAO reports mangoes, mangosteens and guavas as a single commodity group, metric tonnes. India dominates the category.
trivia: India produces more mangoes than the next five countries combined, but exports very little of its crop — most is consumed domestically fresh or as pulp.

title: Largest grape producers
prompt: Name the world's largest grape-producing countries by volume (all uses — table, wine, raisin, juice).

source.name: FAOSTAT — Crops and livestock products

disclaimer: All grape production in metric tonnes — includes table grapes, wine grapes, raisin grapes and juice grapes combined.
trivia: China became the world's largest overall grape grower around 2010, but the vast majority of its crop is eaten as table grapes rather than made into wine, unlike in France or Italy.

title: Largest new-car markets
prompt: Name the countries with the largest new passenger-car sales markets.

source.name: JATO Dynamics / OICA — new passenger car registrations

disclaimer: Ranked by new passenger-car registrations (retail sales) in the reference year, not by production. Light commercial vehicles are excluded.
trivia: The Chinese passenger-car market is roughly twice the size of the U.S. market, and India overtook Japan for third place around 2022.

title: Most Formula 1 team HQs
prompt: Name the countries that host the most Formula 1 constructor team headquarters.

source.name: Formula 1 — Constructor teams

disclaimer: Counts constructors' operational headquarters (chassis factories), not the flag/licence country used for the FIA Constructors' Championship. Small pool: 10 constructor teams total in 2024.
trivia: Seven of the 10 Formula 1 constructors are headquartered in the UK's 'Motorsport Valley' between Oxford and Northampton, including Mercedes, Red Bull, McLaren, Williams, Aston Martin, Alpine (Enstone) and Haas' European base.

title: Largest motorcycle producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most motorcycles and scooters annually.

source.name: Statista / ACEM — global motorcycle production

disclaimer: Total two-wheeler unit production (motorcycles, scooters, mopeds) by country of assembly, not by brand nationality. Includes both domestic-brand and joint-venture output.
trivia: India overtook China around 2017 as the world's largest motorcycle producer, and Hero MotoCorp alone builds roughly 6 million two-wheelers per year.

title: Most electric-bus production
prompt: Name the countries producing the most battery-electric buses per year.

source.name: IEA — Global EV Outlook (electric bus sales/production)

disclaimer: Battery-electric buses only (excludes hybrid, trolleybus, hydrogen fuel-cell). Ranked by units built in-country, which for most markets closely matches domestic deployment.
trivia: China accounts for over 90% of the world's electric-bus fleet; BYD and Yutong alone have built more e-buses than the rest of the world combined.

title: Highest commercial vehicle production
prompt: Name the countries producing the most commercial vehicles (trucks, buses, vans).

source.name: OICA — Commercial Vehicle Production Statistics

disclaimer: OICA commercial-vehicle definition covers light commercial vehicles (LCVs), heavy trucks, and buses, but excludes passenger cars. Country of assembly, not brand nationality.
trivia: China's commercial-vehicle output crashed from 5.2 million in 2016 to 3.4 million in 2022 as heavy-truck demand collapsed with the property downturn, but rebounded in 2023.

title: Most Boeing 737 orders
prompt: Name the countries whose airlines have placed the most orders for the Boeing 737 family.

source.name: Boeing — Orders & Deliveries (737 program)

disclaimer: Cumulative net firm orders for all Boeing 737 variants (Classic, NG, MAX) attributed to the launch customer's country of registration. Leasing companies are attributed to their domicile; unallocated / undisclosed orders are excluded.
trivia: Southwest Airlines is by far the single largest 737 operator, having ordered over 800 aircraft; the U.S. accounts for more than a third of the entire 737 program's cumulative orders.

title: Most Airbus A320 orders
prompt: Name the countries whose airlines have placed the most orders for the Airbus A320 family.

source.name: Airbus — Orders & Deliveries (A320 family)

disclaimer: Cumulative net firm orders for all A320-family variants (A318/A319/A320/A321 including neo). Attributed to airline country of registration; leasing companies attributed to domicile.
trivia: IndiGo and Air India together placed a record-breaking 970 A320-family orders in 2023, pushing India past the U.S. for the single biggest year of narrowbody orders in Airbus history.

title: Largest civilian drone markets
prompt: Name the countries with the largest consumer and commercial drone markets by revenue.

source.name: Statista — Consumer Drones and Commercial UAV Market

disclaimer: Consumer plus commercial civilian drone spend (excludes military UAVs). Revenue-based ranking in USD; hobbyist and enterprise segments combined.
trivia: DJI (Shenzhen) accounts for roughly 70% of global consumer-drone sales, but the U.S. is the single largest end-user market by revenue.

title: Most trucks produced
prompt: Name the countries producing the most heavy trucks (Class 8 / >6-tonne GVW) per year.

source.name: OICA — Truck production statistics

disclaimer: Heavy trucks over 6-tonne GVW (roughly EU N2/N3 and US Classes 5-8) as reported by OICA. Excludes light commercial vehicles and pickups.
trivia: China builds more heavy trucks than the rest of the world combined; Sinotruk, FAW, Dongfeng and Foton each rival Daimler Truck in unit volume.

title: Most auto assembly plants
prompt: Name the countries with the most active passenger-car and light-vehicle assembly plants.

source.name: MarkLines / Automotive News — Global assembly plant database

disclaimer: Active light-vehicle assembly plants (cars, SUVs, LCVs) with reported nameplate capacity in the reference year. Excludes standalone engine, transmission, and body-only facilities.
trivia: Detroit and its suburbs alone have historically hosted more auto plants than any European country; today Guangdong province rivals the entire U.S. Midwest for assembly-plant density.

title: Most FIFA Men's World Cup appearances
prompt: Name the countries that have qualified for the most editions of the FIFA Men's World Cup finals tournament.

source.name: FIFA — World Cup archive

disclaimer: Counts finals-tournament appearances only, not qualifying campaigns. West Germany appearances are combined with unified Germany.
trivia: Brazil is the only nation to have played in every single edition of the men's World Cup.

title: Most goals scored at the Men's World Cup (all-time)
prompt: Name the countries whose national teams have scored the most goals across all editions of the FIFA Men's World Cup finals.

source.name: FIFA — World Cup all-time statistics

disclaimer: Aggregate goals scored in World Cup finals matches only. West Germany goals are combined with Germany.
trivia: Brazil and Germany between them have scored roughly one in every four goals in men's World Cup history.

title: Most UEFA European Championship (Euros) wins
prompt: Name the countries that have won the most UEFA European Championship (Euros) titles.

source.name: UEFA — European Championship history

disclaimer: West Germany's titles are counted under Germany. Soviet Union's title is counted under Russia as its FIFA-recognised successor.
trivia: Spain became the first nation to win four Euros with their 2024 triumph, breaking a tie with Germany.

title: Most Copa America wins
prompt: Name the CONMEBOL nations that have won the most Copa America titles.

source.name: CONMEBOL — Copa America records

disclaimer: Includes titles from the tournament's earlier name (Campeonato Sudamericano) since 1916. Only CONMEBOL members and invitees are eligible; no non-South American nation has ever won.
trivia: Argentina's 2021 and 2024 titles ended a 28-year drought and lifted them past Uruguay for the outright record.

title: Most CAF Africa Cup of Nations wins
prompt: Name the African nations that have won the most CAF Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) titles.

source.name: CAF — Africa Cup of Nations archive

disclaimer: Includes the 1957 inaugural tournament. Egypt's total spans multiple eras of the competition.
trivia: Ivory Coast are the reigning champions after winning AFCON 2023 as hosts, coming back from a group-stage near-elimination.

title: Most AFC Asian Cup wins
prompt: Name the Asian nations that have won the most AFC Asian Cup titles.

source.name: AFC — Asian Cup history
source.asOf: 2024 (through Asian Cup 2023 held in Qatar in early 2024)

trivia: Qatar are back-to-back champions after winning at home in 2019 and successfully defending the title in 2023-24.
asOfDate: 2024 (through Asian Cup 2023 held in Qatar in early 2024)

title: Most CONCACAF Gold Cup / Championship wins
prompt: Name the CONCACAF nations that have won the most regional championships (CONCACAF Championship 1963-1989 and Gold Cup from 1991).

source.name: CONCACAF — Gold Cup archive

trivia: Mexico and the United States have won every Gold Cup since 1991 except for Canada's 2000 upset triumph.

title: Most players in Europe's top 5 leagues
prompt: Name the countries producing the most players in Europe's Big Five leagues (Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga, Ligue 1).

source.name: CIES Football Observatory — Big-5 League Demographic Study

disclaimer: Counts unique senior players who appeared in at least one league fixture during the season, by country of birth. English, Scottish, Welsh and Northern Irish players are consolidated under United Kingdom.
trivia: France exports more Big-5 talent than any other single nation state, with more French-born players outside Ligue 1 than inside it.

title: Most FIFA Confederations Cup wins
prompt: Name the countries that have won the most FIFA Confederations Cup titles (1992-2017).

source.name: FIFA — Confederations Cup archive

disclaimer: Includes the 1992 and 1995 King Fahd Cup editions that FIFA recognises as part of the competition's lineage.
trivia: Brazil won four Confederations Cups but never converted the form into a World Cup title in any of the same cycles.

title: Most FIFA U-20 World Cup wins
prompt: Name the countries that have won the most FIFA U-20 (Under-20) Men's World Cup titles.

source.name: FIFA — U-20 World Cup archive

disclaimer: Formerly known as the FIFA World Youth Championship (1977-2005). Soviet Union titles are counted under Russia.
trivia: Uruguay's 2023 triumph gave a South American country the U-20 title for the first time since Argentina's 2007 win.

title: Largest Exclusive Economic Zone
prompt: Name the countries with the largest maritime Exclusive Economic Zone (EEZ), the ocean territory extending 200 nautical miles from a nation's coasts.

source.name: Sea Around Us / Flanders Marine Institute (VLIZ) — MarineRegions.org

disclaimer: Includes EEZs of overseas territories, dependencies, and outlying islands attributed to the administering sovereign state. Overlapping/disputed claims are counted for both parties.
trivia: France's EEZ narrowly beats the United States' largely because of its Pacific territories — French Polynesia alone accounts for about 4.8 million km² of it.

title: Most islands
prompt: Name the countries with the most islands (including small islets and skerries counted in national geographic surveys).

source.name: National geographic surveys (Statistics Sweden, Finnish Environment Institute, Statistics Norway, Statistics Canada, etc.)

disclaimer: Definitions vary widely — some counts include any land above high tide, others require a minimum area or vegetation. Rankings use each country's own official inventory.
trivia: Sweden's official count includes nearly 222,000 skerries barely poking above the Baltic — most have no name and can't be landed on.

title: Flattest terrain (lowest peak)
prompt: Name the countries with the flattest terrain, measured by the lowest elevation of their highest point.

prompt: Name the countries with the highest score on the Social Progress Index, measuring basic human needs, wellbeing, and opportunity.

source.name: Social Progress Imperative — Social Progress Index

disclaimer: SPI is a 0-100 composite that intentionally excludes GDP and other economic indicators, focusing on social and environmental outcomes such as nutrition, sanitation, personal safety, health, environmental quality, personal rights, and inclusiveness.
trivia: The index was created by Michael Porter and Scott Stern of Harvard/MIT to give governments a non-economic measure of national success. Nordic countries have topped it every year since it launched in 2013.

title: Highest social spending as % of GDP
prompt: Name the countries with the highest public social spending as a share of GDP.

source.name: OECD — Social Expenditure Database (SOCX)

disclaimer: Public social spending covers cash benefits and in-kind services in old age, survivors, incapacity, health, family, active labour market programs, unemployment, housing, and other social areas. OECD member countries only; comparable data are not published for non-members.
trivia: France has been the OECD's highest social spender almost every year since the late 1990s, with pensions and health the two largest components. The US ranks mid-table by public spending but rises to near the top if private social spending (mostly employer health plans) is included.

title: Highest child labor rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of children aged 5-17 engaged in child labour.

source.name: ILO / UNICEF — Child Labour: Global estimates and country data
source.asOf: Most recent MICS/DHS survey per country, 2018-2023

disclaimer: Child labour is defined by the ILO as work that deprives children of their childhood, potential and dignity, and is harmful to physical or mental development. Countries with no recent household survey (e.g. many high-income OECD states) are not comparable and are excluded.
trivia: The ILO estimates about 160 million children worldwide were in child labour as of 2020 — the first rise in two decades, largely attributed to the COVID-19 pandemic. West and Central Africa have the highest regional rate.
asOfDate: Most recent MICS/DHS survey per country, 2018-2023

title: Highest LGBTI+ acceptance
prompt: Name the countries where public acceptance of LGBTI+ people is highest according to the Global Acceptance Index.

source.name: Williams Institute (UCLA) — Global Acceptance Index
source.asOf: 2021 update, based on Gallup / WVS / ISSP polling

disclaimer: The Global Acceptance Index is a 0-10 composite of survey responses on attitudes toward gay/lesbian people, same-sex marriage, transgender rights, and LGBTI policy from Gallup, the World Values Survey, and the ISSP.
trivia: The Williams Institute's index has found a growing global divide since the 2010s: the most-accepting countries have become steadily more accepting, while the least-accepting have become more hostile, with roughly half the world's countries backsliding.
asOfDate: 2021 update, based on Gallup / WVS / ISSP polling

title: Highest World Giving Index
prompt: Name the countries with the highest score on the CAF World Giving Index, measuring generosity through helping strangers, donating money, and volunteering.

source.name: Charities Aid Foundation — World Giving Index

disclaimer: The index is a 0-100 score averaging the share of adults who, in the past month, helped a stranger, donated money to charity, and volunteered time with an organisation.
trivia: Indonesia has topped the CAF World Giving Index every year from 2017 through the 2023 edition — driven largely by mosque-based zakat charity, which produces the highest donation-participation rate in the world.

title: Highest Quality of Life Index (Numbeo)
prompt: Name the countries with the highest score on the Numbeo Quality of Life Index, a crowdsourced composite of purchasing power, safety, healthcare, cost of living, housing, commute, pollution, and climate.

source.name: Numbeo — Quality of Life Index by Country

disclaimer: Numbeo's index is aggregated from user-submitted survey data rather than official statistics; a higher score is better. Very small countries with few submissions are excluded by Numbeo's minimum-sample threshold.
trivia: Numbeo's data set is one of the largest crowdsourced cost-of-living surveys in the world, with over half a million respondents contributing entries each year — the index is widely referenced by expat and relocation media even though academics prefer OECD Better Life or SPI.

title: Highest homelessness rate per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest rate of homelessness per capita.

source.name: OECD Affordable Housing Database — HC3.1 Homeless population
source.asOf: Most recent national point-in-time count per country, 2019-2023

disclaimer: Definitions of homelessness vary widely across countries and comparisons are approximate. Values are per 10,000 residents; countries without a recent national homeless census are excluded.
trivia: New Zealand's high ranking reflects the broadest official definition in the OECD, which includes people living in severely crowded housing or emergency accommodation as well as those without shelter — narrower definitions would move the US to the top of this list.
asOfDate: Most recent national point-in-time count per country, 2019-2023

title: Most unicorn startups
prompt: Name the countries hosting the most unicorn startups (private companies valued over $1B).

source.name: CB Insights — The Complete List of Unicorn Companies

disclaimer: Ranked by country of headquarters at the time of unicorn valuation. Cross-listed dual-HQ startups are attributed to their primary operating country.
trivia: The US alone accounts for more than half of all unicorns tracked by CB Insights, driven by Bay Area and NYC concentration.

title: Most Fortune Global 500 tech companies
prompt: Name the countries with the most Fortune Global 500 companies in the technology sector.

source.name: Fortune Global 500 — Technology sector

disclaimer: Counts firms classified under Fortune's Technology, Internet Services & Retailing, and Computers/Office Equipment industry categories.
trivia: China and the US together account for roughly three-quarters of Fortune's Global 500 tech firms.

title: Largest semiconductor fab capacity
prompt: Name the countries with the largest semiconductor fabrication (wafer) capacity.

source.name: SEMI World Fab Forecast / Statista

disclaimer: Measured in 200mm-equivalent monthly wafer capacity across all technology nodes and product types (memory, logic, analog).
trivia: Taiwan hosts TSMC's leading-edge fabs while South Korea's total is dominated by Samsung and SK Hynix memory fabs.

title: Most software developers
prompt: Name the countries with the largest population of professional software developers.

source.name: GitHub Octoverse / SlashData Developer Economics / Statista

disclaimer: Estimates from developer platform data (GitHub accounts, LinkedIn listings, industry surveys) — actual professional employment figures may vary between sources.
trivia: India overtook the US in GitHub developer count in 2024 and is projected to lead globally by 2028 on that metric.

title: Most AI patent filings
prompt: Name the countries filing the most artificial intelligence patents.

source.name: WIPO — Patent Landscape Report on Generative AI

disclaimer: Counts patent families with at least one AI-related claim filed between 2014 and 2023, attributed to inventor's country of residence.
trivia: China alone accounts for over 70% of global generative AI patent filings between 2014 and 2023, per WIPO.

title: Most data centers
prompt: Name the countries hosting the most colocation data centers.

source.name: Cloudscene — Global Data Center Marketplace

disclaimer: Counts commercial multi-tenant colocation facilities listed on Cloudscene. Enterprise-owned hyperscale campuses (Google, Meta, AWS) are not fully represented in this dataset.
trivia: The US hosts more colocation data centers than the next five countries combined; Northern Virginia alone holds around 300 facilities.

title: Largest venture capital funding
prompt: Name the countries attracting the most annual venture capital investment.

source.name: KPMG Venture Pulse / PitchBook

disclaimer: Measured in USD across all deal stages (seed, early, late) where the startup is headquartered in the listed country. Excludes secondary transactions.
trivia: US venture funding equalled roughly the combined total of every other country on Earth in 2023.

title: Most Y Combinator-backed startups
prompt: Name the countries producing the most Y Combinator-backed startups.

source.name: Y Combinator — Company Directory

disclaimer: Counts startups by founding-team country of primary operation, not incorporation. Batches counted through Winter 2024.
trivia: India overtook Canada as YC's second-largest source country in 2023, driven by heavy fintech and SaaS batches.

title: Largest tech stock market cap
prompt: Name the countries whose stock exchanges host the largest aggregate technology-sector market capitalisation.

source.name: Statista / WFE — Technology sector market capitalisation by exchange

disclaimer: Measured in USD by primary listing country. Dual-listed firms (e.g. Alibaba on NYSE and HKEX) are counted only where their primary listing is registered.
trivia: The US NASDAQ alone accounts for more listed tech market cap than every other exchange on Earth combined, driven by the Mag 7.

title: Highest software engineer salaries
prompt: Name the countries with the highest average annual salary for software engineers.

source.name: Levels.fyi — Country Compensation Report

disclaimer: Median total compensation (base + bonus + stock) for software engineers in USD, based on self-reported Levels.fyi submissions. Skewed toward employees at large tech firms; smaller-company medians are lower.
trivia: Switzerland tops many mid-career salary tables, but US total comp wins overall thanks to equity grants at FAANG-tier firms.

title: Largest goods importers
prompt: Name the countries that import the most merchandise (goods) by total value in USD.

source.name: WTO — World Trade Statistical Review / Trade Statistics

disclaimer: Merchandise (goods) imports only, in current USD. Services trade excluded. EU member states counted separately, not as a bloc.
trivia: The United States has run the world's largest goods import bill nearly every year since 1976, when it overtook West Germany.

title: Largest services exporters
prompt: Name the countries that export the most commercial services by total value in USD.

source.name: WTO — Services trade statistics

disclaimer: Commercial services exports (travel, transport, financial, IT, IP charges, etc.) in current USD. Excludes government services.
trivia: India climbed into the top 5 largely on IT and business-process outsourcing exports, which alone crossed $200B in 2023.

title: Largest services importers
prompt: Name the countries that import the most commercial services by total value in USD.

source.name: WTO — Services trade statistics

disclaimer: Commercial services imports (travel, transport, financial, IT, IP charges, etc.) in current USD. Excludes government services.
trivia: Ireland's services import bill is inflated by multinationals routing intellectual-property royalty payments through Irish subsidiaries.

title: Highest FDI inflows (annual)
prompt: Name the countries that attracted the most foreign direct investment (FDI) inflows in a recent year.

source.name: UNCTAD — World Investment Report

disclaimer: Annual FDI inflows (net) in current USD. Includes equity, reinvested earnings, and intra-company debt. Values swing year to year; ranked by 2023 report.
trivia: Luxembourg and the Netherlands regularly appear because multinationals route capital through their favorable holding-company regimes, not because of real productive investment.

title: Largest inward FDI stock
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total accumulated stock of foreign direct investment held inside their borders.

source.name: UNCTAD — World Investment Report / FDI stocks database

disclaimer: Cumulative inward FDI stock in current USD. Small conduit economies (BVI, Cayman) excluded — only sovereign countries in the answer set.
trivia: The Netherlands hosts the world's largest inward FDI stock per capita, mostly attributable to Special Financial Institutions used by multinationals.

title: Largest current account surpluses
prompt: Name the countries with the largest current account surpluses by USD value.

source.name: IMF — World Economic Outlook / Balance of Payments Statistics

disclaimer: Absolute USD current account surplus (goods + services + primary income + secondary income). Ranks countries in surplus only; deficit countries excluded.
trivia: Germany's current account surplus has been criticized by the IMF and European Commission as excessive relative to its share of eurozone GDP.

title: Largest current account deficits
prompt: Name the countries with the largest current account deficits by USD value.

source.name: IMF — World Economic Outlook / Balance of Payments Statistics

disclaimer: Absolute USD current account deficit. Ranked from largest deficit (most negative) to smallest. Surplus countries excluded.
trivia: The US has run a current account deficit every year since 1982, but as a share of GDP it has narrowed from a 2006 peak near 6% to under 3.5%.

title: Highest economic complexity
prompt: Name the countries with the highest Economic Complexity Index (ECI) — a measure of the diversity and sophistication of exports.

source.name: Harvard Growth Lab — Atlas of Economic Complexity

disclaimer: Economic Complexity Index (ECI) measures export sophistication and diversity. Higher = more complex. Petro-states and single-commodity exporters score low regardless of GDP.
trivia: Japan has led the ECI rankings every year since the index was created in the 1960s — driven by dominance in precision machinery, electronics and chemicals.

title: Largest US trading partners
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total two-way goods trade with the United States.

source.name: US Census Bureau — Foreign Trade / USTR

disclaimer: Two-way merchandise trade in USD (US exports to + US imports from). Excludes services. The US itself is obviously excluded as an answer.
trivia: Mexico overtook China as the largest US trading partner in 2023 for the first time in over 20 years, driven by nearshoring and higher US tariffs on Chinese goods.

title: Largest domestic aviation market
prompt: Name the countries with the largest domestic aviation markets, measured by domestic revenue passenger kilometres (RPK) flown within the country.

source.name: ICAO — Air Transport Statistics (domestic scheduled RPK)

disclaimer: Measures scheduled domestic traffic only (city-pairs within the same country). Big-geography countries with high internal air demand dominate.
trivia: The US domestic market alone accounts for more RPKs than the next four countries combined, and China briefly overtook it during 2020 when international travel collapsed.

title: Busiest air cargo hubs
prompt: Name the countries whose airports collectively handle the most air cargo tonnage per year.

source.name: ACI — World Airport Traffic Report (cargo tonnes)

disclaimer: Counts loaded plus unloaded freight tonnes at all commercial airports in the country. Transshipment hubs rank higher than the size of their domestic economy would suggest.
trivia: Hong Kong International (HKG) has been the world's single busiest cargo airport most years since 2010, with Memphis (FedEx) and Anchorage (fuel-stop transshipment) rounding out the top three.

title: Largest airline groups by revenue
prompt: Name the countries that are home to the world's largest airline groups by annual revenue.

source.name: IATA / Airline Business — World Airline Rankings (revenue)

disclaimer: Ranked by combined annual revenue of airline groups headquartered in the country (e.g. Delta, United, American together for the US). Excludes cargo-only carriers.
trivia: Delta, American and United each individually cleared $50B in 2023 — no other country hosts even one carrier that large, though Lufthansa Group and Air France-KLM lead in Europe.

title: Most Boeing 787 Dreamliners in service
prompt: Name the countries whose airlines operate the most Boeing 787 Dreamliner aircraft in commercial service.

source.name: Boeing / Cirium Fleets Analyzer (787 in-service fleet by operator country)

disclaimer: Counts in-service 787-8/9/10 airframes with airlines headquartered in the country. Aircraft on order but not delivered are excluded.
trivia: ANA of Japan took delivery of the very first 787 in 2011 and remains one of the largest operators; United and American between them fly well over 100.

title: Largest widebody airliner fleets
prompt: Name the countries whose airlines operate the most widebody (twin-aisle) passenger aircraft.

source.name: Cirium Fleets Analyzer — widebody in-service fleet by operator country

disclaimer: Includes A330, A340, A350, A380, 747, 767, 777 and 787 in commercial passenger service. Freighter versions of the same types are excluded.
trivia: The three biggest Gulf carriers (Emirates, Qatar, Etihad) between them fly more widebodies than all of Latin America combined, and Emirates alone operates the world's largest A380 fleet.

title: Largest regional-jet fleets
prompt: Name the countries whose airlines operate the most regional jets (50-100 seat aircraft such as the Embraer E-Jet and Bombardier CRJ families).

source.name: Cirium Fleets Analyzer — regional jets in service by operator country

disclaimer: Includes Embraer ERJ/E-Jet, Bombardier CRJ, Mitsubishi/CRJ, Sukhoi Superjet and Comac ARJ21. Excludes turboprops and mainline narrowbodies.
trivia: The US alone flies over half the world's regional jets — mostly Embraer E175s and CRJs operating for regional affiliates of American, Delta and United.

title: Safest national airline industries (JACDEC)
prompt: Name the countries whose commercial airlines rank safest overall in JACDEC's Airline Safety Index (i.e. lowest weighted accident/incident risk scores).

source.name: JACDEC — Airline Safety Index (country aggregation)

disclaimer: Rank 1 is safest. Index blends 30-year weighted accident history, serious incident rate, fleet age and audit ratings. Countries whose airlines dominate the top-25 list score best.
trivia: Emirates, Qatar Airways and Cathay Pacific have all held the individual #1 slot at various points, and Qantas famously used a clean fatal-accident record as a marketing point for decades.

title: Most airline accidents 2000-2024
prompt: Name the countries with the most commercial airline hull-loss or fatal accidents recorded between 2000 and 2024.

source.name: Aviation Safety Network — ASN Accident Database

disclaimer: Counts hull-loss and fatal accidents to airliners of 12+ seats, by country of occurrence (not by airline nationality). Includes both scheduled passenger and cargo operations.
trivia: Russia and the DRC together account for a disproportionate share of the ASN list — Russia because of its huge fleet and geography, the DRC because of a long tail of small operators flying ageing Antonov and Boeing 727 equipment.

title: Largest general aviation fleets
prompt: Name the countries with the most general aviation aircraft (private jets, piston singles/twins, business turboprops and light aircraft) on their civil registries.

source.name: GAMA — General Aviation Statistical Databook & Industry Outlook

disclaimer: General aviation excludes scheduled airline and military aircraft. Counts active registrations on the national civil register.
trivia: The FAA registry lists more than 200,000 active general aviation aircraft — more than the rest of the world combined — a legacy of the postwar boom in private flying and the density of US uncontrolled airfields.

title: Largest space agency budgets
prompt: Name the countries whose national civil space programs have the largest annual budgets.

source.name: OECD — The Space Economy in Figures / national space-agency budget filings

disclaimer: Government civil space spending only (NASA, ESA member states, JAXA, CNSA, ISRO, Roscosmos etc.). Excludes military space budgets and private-sector spending. Chinese and Russian figures are estimated.
trivia: NASA's budget of roughly $25B is more than the next five national space agencies combined, and China's CNSA is the fastest-growing — its true spending is thought to be well above the officially disclosed number.

title: Highest corporate tax rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest statutory corporate income tax rate.

source.name: KPMG — Corporate Tax Rates Table

disclaimer: Statutory headline national corporate income tax rate; excludes surtaxes and subnational levies. Excludes jurisdictions with no corporate income tax.
trivia: Comoros levies a special rate on public industrial and commercial companies, and Puerto Rico's high rate reflects a graduated system on top of federal US tax obligations.

title: Highest personal income tax top rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest top statutory personal income tax rate.

source.name: KPMG — Individual Income Tax Rates Table

disclaimer: Top marginal statutory rate on employment income at the national level. Excludes mandatory social security contributions and local/municipal surcharges.
trivia: In Denmark and Finland, effective top marginal rates including municipal taxes and church tax can exceed 55 percent.

title: Most billionaires per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the most billionaires per million residents.

source.name: Forbes World's Billionaires List

disclaimer: Ratio of Forbes-listed billionaires (net worth USD 1B+) to national population. Small tax-haven jurisdictions dominate; the list excludes SARs like Hong Kong and Macao.
trivia: Monaco has by far the highest concentration on the planet — a single billionaire in Monaco already produces a rate over 20 per million.

title: Most self-employed workforce
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of workers who are self-employed.

source.name: ILOSTAT — Status in employment

disclaimer: Self-employed as a percent of total employment, ILO modelled estimates. Includes own-account workers, employers, and contributing family workers.
trivia: In many high-ranking African economies, subsistence agriculture pushes self-employment above 80 percent of the labor force.

title: Most Nobel laureates in Economics
prompt: Name the countries with the most Nobel Prize in Economic Sciences laureates by nationality.

source.name: The Nobel Prize — All Prizes in Economic Sciences

disclaimer: The Sveriges Riksbank Prize in Economic Sciences in Memory of Alfred Nobel; counted by laureate country of citizenship at time of award. Dual citizens counted for each nationality.
trivia: The Economics prize is the youngest of the Nobel awards, first given in 1969, and roughly two-thirds of all laureates have held US affiliation at the time of their award.

title: Highest tax revenue as % of GDP
prompt: Name the countries with the highest total tax revenue as a percentage of GDP.

source.name: OECD — Revenue Statistics

disclaimer: Total tax revenue (all levels of government) divided by GDP. Restricted to OECD member countries; the OECD dataset does not cover all countries worldwide.
trivia: Nordic countries dominate the top of the list — Denmark and France have alternated the OECD's #1 tax-to-GDP ranking for most of the past decade.

title: Longest average work week
prompt: Name the countries where employed people work the longest average hours per week.

source.name: ILOSTAT — Mean weekly hours actually worked per employed person

disclaimer: Mean weekly hours actually worked per employed person, all industries, from ILO's harmonized labour force statistics.
trivia: In several top-ranked economies, six-day work weeks are still standard in construction, retail, and small-business sectors.

title: Shortest average work week
prompt: Name the countries where employed people work the fewest average hours per week.

source.name: ILOSTAT — Mean weekly hours actually worked per employed person

disclaimer: Mean weekly hours actually worked per employed person across all industries. Includes both full- and part-time workers, which pulls averages down where part-time work is widespread.
trivia: The Netherlands has one of the world's highest shares of part-time employment — roughly half of all Dutch workers are part-time, which is why its weekly hours are so low.

title: Strongest employment protection
prompt: Name the countries with the strictest employment protection laws for regular workers.

source.name: OECD — Employment Protection Legislation Index

disclaimer: OECD EPL index for individual dismissals of regular contract workers on a 0-6 scale where higher means stricter protection. Only OECD-covered countries.
trivia: The index has three sub-components: procedural inconveniences, notice/severance rules, and the difficulty of dismissal — high-ranking countries typically require judicial approval before firing.

title: Most deaths from natural disasters (2000-2024)
prompt: Name the countries with the highest total deaths from natural disasters since 2000.

source.name: EM-DAT — The International Disaster Database (CRED)

disclaimer: Includes geophysical, hydrological, meteorological, climatological and biological disasters as recorded by EM-DAT. Excludes disease outbreaks (COVID-19) and conflict deaths.
trivia: The 2010 Haiti earthquake and 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami are the two single deadliest events in the EM-DAT record for this period, together accounting for over 450,000 deaths.

title: Highest World Risk Index
prompt: Name the countries with the highest disaster risk on the World Risk Index.

source.name: World Risk Report — Bündnis Entwicklung Hilft / IFHV Ruhr-University Bochum

disclaimer: The WorldRiskIndex combines exposure to natural hazards with societal vulnerability (susceptibility, coping and adaptive capacity). Higher score = higher risk.
trivia: The Philippines has ranked #1 on the WorldRiskIndex in most editions since 2011, driven by high exposure to typhoons, earthquakes and sea-level rise combined with dense coastal populations.

title: Most active volcanoes
prompt: Name the countries with the most Holocene active volcanoes.

source.name: Smithsonian Institution — Global Volcanism Program

disclaimer: Counts volcanoes with confirmed Holocene (last 10,000 years) eruptions. A country can host many volcanoes on a single island arc.
trivia: The United States' count is dominated by Alaska's Aleutian Arc and Cascades; Indonesia's Sunda Arc packs the world's densest chain of active volcanoes.

title: Most affected by earthquakes (deaths since 1900)
prompt: Name the countries with the highest cumulative earthquake death tolls in the modern record.

source.name: EM-DAT / USGS Significant Earthquake Database

disclaimer: Cumulative deaths from earthquakes (including tsunamis triggered by them) since 1900. Includes the 1976 Tangshan, 2004 Sumatra-Andaman, 2010 Haiti, 2008 Sichuan and 2023 Turkey-Syria events.
trivia: The 1976 Tangshan earthquake (~242,000 official Chinese deaths) and the 1920 Haiyuan quake (~235,000) place China at the top of most 20th-21st century tallies.

title: Most affected by tropical cyclones
prompt: Name the countries with the highest cumulative death tolls from tropical cyclones (hurricanes/typhoons).

source.name: EM-DAT — Storms subgroup

disclaimer: Cumulative deaths from tropical cyclones — hurricanes in the Atlantic/E. Pacific, typhoons in the NW Pacific, and cyclones in the Indian Ocean / S. Pacific.
trivia: The 1970 Bhola cyclone (then East Pakistan, now Bangladesh) killed an estimated 300,000-500,000 people — the deadliest tropical cyclone on record.

title: Most affected by floods (deaths since 1900)
prompt: Name the countries with the highest cumulative death tolls from floods.

source.name: EM-DAT — Floods subgroup

disclaimer: Cumulative flood deaths (riverine, flash and coastal). The 1931 China floods alone are estimated to have killed 1-4 million people, dominating any long-run ranking.
trivia: China's 1931, 1935, and 1959 Yellow/Yangtze River floods together caused more deaths than every other natural disaster in the 20th century combined by some estimates.

title: Highest financial cost of natural disasters
prompt: Name the countries with the largest cumulative economic damages from natural disasters.

source.name: EM-DAT — Total damages (US$)

disclaimer: Reported direct economic damages in nominal US dollars as logged in EM-DAT. Rich, disaster-prone countries dominate simply because reported damages scale with insured asset values.
trivia: Hurricane Katrina (2005), Superstorm Sandy (2012), Hurricane Harvey (2017), and the 2011 Tohoku earthquake/tsunami are the four costliest single events on record.

title: Highest famine / acute food insecurity risk
prompt: Name the countries with the largest populations in IPC Phase 3+ (Crisis or worse) acute food insecurity.

source.name: IPC — Integrated Food Security Phase Classification

disclaimer: Population in IPC/CH Phase 3 (Crisis), Phase 4 (Emergency) or Phase 5 (Catastrophe/Famine). Conflict and drought are the main drivers.
trivia: Sudan's 2024 crisis is the first time an IPC Famine (Phase 5) classification has been officially declared in Sudan; Gaza was also classified in Phase 5 areas.

title: Most refugees produced (source countries)
prompt: Name the countries producing the largest refugee populations displaced abroad.

source.name: UNHCR — Refugee Data Finder

disclaimer: Counts refugees, asylum-seekers, and others in need of international protection who originate from each country (i.e. source, not host). Excludes internally displaced people (IDPs).
trivia: Syria was the world's top refugee-producing country every year from 2014 through 2023, until the 2022 Russia-Ukraine war briefly made Ukraine the largest single-year outflow.

title: Most Ebola cases historically
prompt: Name the countries with the most cumulative recorded Ebola virus disease cases.

source.name: WHO — Ebola outbreak situation reports

disclaimer: Cumulative confirmed and probable Ebola virus disease cases across all outbreaks. The 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak dominates the totals.
trivia: The 2014-2016 West Africa outbreak was the largest in history, with over 28,000 cases and 11,000 deaths — before that, no single outbreak had exceeded 425 cases.

title: Largest informal/shadow economy
prompt: Name the countries where the informal (shadow/gray) economy is the largest share of GDP.

source.name: IMF Working Paper — Shadow Economies Around the World (Medina & Schneider)

disclaimer: Shadow economy as a percentage of official GDP. Includes unreported cash work, small unregistered businesses and legal activities hidden from tax authorities; excludes illegal activities (drugs, smuggling).
trivia: Even advanced OECD economies typically sit in the 8–15% range, while resource-poor developing countries can exceed 50% because informal microenterprises absorb most employment.

title: Most tourism-reliant economies
prompt: Name the countries where travel and tourism contribute the largest share of GDP.

source.name: World Travel & Tourism Council — Economic Impact Reports

disclaimer: Total contribution of travel and tourism to GDP (direct plus indirect and induced), as a percentage. Small island states dominate because tourism revenue swamps a tiny domestic economy.
trivia: For several Caribbean and Pacific microstates, more than one full-time job in three depends on tourism, which is why COVID-era border closures triggered double-digit GDP contractions there.

title: Most remittance-reliant economies
prompt: Name the countries where personal remittances from workers abroad make up the largest share of GDP.

source.name: World Bank — Migration and Remittances Data

disclaimer: Personal remittances received as percentage of GDP. Reflects money sent home by nationals working abroad, a common lifeline for economies with heavy labor migration.
trivia: Remittances to low- and middle-income countries now exceed foreign direct investment in aggregate, and for Tajikistan they routinely rival government tax revenue.

title: Most foreign-aid-reliant economies
prompt: Name the countries where net official development assistance (foreign aid) is the largest share of gross national income.

source.name: World Bank — Net ODA received (% of GNI)

disclaimer: Net official development assistance (ODA) as a percentage of gross national income. Includes grants and concessional loans from DAC donors and multilateral agencies; excludes military aid.
trivia: Micronesia, Marshall Islands and Palau receive aid mainly through Compacts of Free Association with the United States, an arrangement unique to the North Pacific.

title: Highest agriculture share of GDP
prompt: Name the countries where agriculture, forestry and fishing contribute the largest share of GDP.

source.name: World Bank — Agriculture, forestry and fishing, value added (% of GDP)

disclaimer: Value added from agriculture, forestry and fishing as a share of GDP. Rich countries typically sit below 3%; economies still transitioning out of subsistence farming often exceed 25%.
trivia: Sierra Leone's agricultural share spiked after the civil war knocked mining and services offline, and cassava, rice and cocoa remain the workhorse crops.

title: Highest industrial share of GDP
prompt: Name the countries where industry (mining, manufacturing, construction and utilities) contributes the largest share of GDP.

source.name: World Bank — Industry (including construction), value added (% of GDP)

disclaimer: Industry value added as a share of GDP, which includes mining, manufacturing, construction and utilities. Petrostates dominate the top of the list because oil and gas extraction is booked here.
trivia: Ireland's share is inflated by multinational manufacturing (pharmaceuticals, semiconductors, tech IP) booked through its corporate tax regime rather than by heavy industry on the ground.

title: Highest services share of GDP
prompt: Name the countries where the services sector contributes the largest share of GDP.

source.name: World Bank — Services, value added (% of GDP)

disclaimer: Services value added as a share of GDP, covering finance, tourism, trade, transport, government and personal services. Small tax-and-tourism economies dominate; strict microstates like Monaco are excluded because World Bank does not report a full series.
trivia: Djibouti's economy runs on port and transhipment services for landlocked Ethiopia, giving it a service share that looks like a tourism microstate despite little actual tourism.

title: Largest agriculture labor force share
prompt: Name the countries where the largest share of workers are employed in agriculture (the primary sector).

source.name: World Bank — Employment in agriculture (% of total employment, ILO modelled estimate)

disclaimer: Modelled ILO estimate of employment in agriculture, forestry and fishing as percentage of total employment. Reflects subsistence and smallholder farming, not just commercial agribusiness.
trivia: In much of the Sahel, official labor-force numbers understate rural work because a large share of women's farm labor is unpaid family labor that some household surveys miss.

title: Largest merchant marine flag registries
prompt: Name the countries whose flag registries carry the most merchant shipping tonnage (open registries / flags of convenience dominate).

source.name: UNCTAD Review of Maritime Transport — Merchant fleet by flag of registration

disclaimer: Deadweight tonnage of the merchant fleet registered under each flag. Open registries (flags of convenience) let foreign shipowners register vessels, so top ranks bear little relation to the underlying beneficial owners.
trivia: Panama has led global flag registries since the 1990s; the Liberian registry is administered from Virginia, USA, under a private corporate concession rather than from Monrovia.

title: Biggest global tax havens
prompt: Name the jurisdictions that enable the most corporate tax abuse according to the Tax Justice Network's Corporate Tax Haven Index.

source.name: Tax Justice Network — Corporate Tax Haven Index

disclaimer: Ranking based on the Corporate Tax Haven Index score, which combines a jurisdiction's tax-haven aggressiveness with its share of global corporate financial activity. Higher score = more enabling of profit shifting.
trivia: The British Virgin Islands, Cayman Islands and Bermuda have topped the list for years despite tiny populations, because they host trillions of dollars of shell-company assets registered by multinationals headquartered elsewhere.

title: Most Rhodes Scholars all-time
prompt: Name the countries that have produced the most Rhodes Scholars (Oxford) since the scholarship's founding in 1902.

source.name: Rhodes Trust — Scholar constituencies

disclaimer: Counts by Scholar's home constituency at time of award. Constituencies have shifted over the decades (e.g., separate German scholarships were suspended in the World Wars).
trivia: Cecil Rhodes designed the scholarship originally for 20 U.S. state constituencies, four Australian ones, and one each for a handful of British Empire jurisdictions — a footprint that has since expanded to more than 20 constituencies worldwide.

title: Most Fulbright grants by home country
prompt: Name the countries that send the most Fulbright Program grantees to the United States each year (visiting scholars and students combined).

source.name: U.S. Department of State — Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs, Fulbright Program annual data

disclaimer: Counts foreign grantees hosted in the U.S. under the Fulbright Foreign Student and Visiting Scholar programs; excludes U.S. Fulbrighters going abroad. Program sizes are set bilaterally, so counts partly reflect commission funding.
trivia: The Fulbright Program operates in more than 160 countries; Germany's Fulbright Commission — established in 1952 — is one of the oldest and consistently one of the largest.

title: Highest tertiary graduation rate (25-34)
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of 25-34 year olds holding a tertiary (post-secondary) qualification.

source.name: OECD — Education at a Glance 2024, Table A1.2

disclaimer: Share of the 25-34 age cohort with a completed tertiary qualification (short-cycle, bachelor's, master's, or doctoral). Restricted to OECD and partner countries reporting to UNESCO/OECD/Eurostat.
trivia: The OECD average for this cohort passed 47% in 2023 — up from 27% in 2000 — reflecting one of the fastest cross-country expansions of higher education in recorded history.

title: Highest STEM graduation share
prompt: Name the countries where STEM fields (science, technology, engineering, mathematics) make up the largest share of tertiary graduates.

source.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics / OECD Education at a Glance — Distribution of tertiary graduates by field

disclaimer: Share of all first-degree tertiary graduates in Natural Sciences, Mathematics & Statistics, ICT, and Engineering/Manufacturing/Construction fields combined. Excludes health/medical.
trivia: Germany's engineering-heavy university system pushes its STEM graduate share above 35% — roughly double the share seen in the U.S. and Canada, where business and humanities enrollments are much larger.

title: Highest primary school completion rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest primary-school completion rates — the share of the relevant age cohort finishing the last grade of primary.

source.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics / World Bank EdStats — Primary completion rate, total (% of relevant age group)

disclaimer: Values above 100% occur when over-age or under-age students complete primary in a given year — an artefact of the ratio methodology, not extra people. Some high-income countries with universal completion don't report every year; those aren't shown.
trivia: The primary completion indicator has been UNESCO's headline Education-for-All metric since 1990 and is directly baked into UN Sustainable Development Goal 4.1.

title: Highest lower-secondary completion rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest lower-secondary school completion rates (share of the relevant age cohort finishing lower-secondary).

source.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics / World Bank EdStats — Lower-secondary completion rate

disclaimer: Rates above 100% reflect over-age or repeat completers within the reference age band — a UIS ratio artefact, not extra pupils.
trivia: Universal lower-secondary completion by 2030 is a formal SDG 4 target; more than 60 countries were still below 80% as recently as 2020.

title: Most primary teachers per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the most primary-school teachers relative to their total population.

source.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics — Teachers in primary education, headcount / UN Population Division

disclaimer: Teachers per 1,000 population, derived from UIS teacher headcount and UN mid-year population. Some jurisdictions with youthful populations and low pupil-teacher ratios (e.g., Cuba) rank high on this metric.
trivia: Cuba has one of the world's lowest pupil-teacher ratios at the primary level (around 9:1), a legacy of the 1961 literacy campaign that put over 100,000 volunteer teachers in the field within a single year.

title: Highest gender parity in secondary education
prompt: Name the countries with the highest female-to-male gender parity index in secondary school enrolment (values above 1.00 favour female enrolment).

source.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics — Gender Parity Index (GPI), Gross enrolment ratio, secondary

disclaimer: GPI is female GER divided by male GER; a value of 1.00 = parity, above 1.00 = more girls than boys in secondary. This list ranks by the largest positive gap in favour of girls, not by absolute enrolment.
trivia: In more than 100 countries the GPI now exceeds 1.00 at the secondary level — a reversal of the mid-20th-century pattern and one of the fastest documented shifts in modern demography.

title: Largest primary school class size
prompt: Name the countries with the largest average primary-school class sizes.

source.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics — Pupil-teacher ratio, primary (as class-size proxy)

disclaimer: Values are pupil-teacher ratios (pupils per teacher), used by UIS as the standard cross-national class-size proxy. Actual class sizes may differ where team-teaching or multi-grade classrooms are common.
trivia: Sub-Saharan Africa's primary pupil-teacher ratio has stayed above 35:1 for two decades — one of the last regions where meeting SDG 4's teacher-supply target remains uncertain.

title: Highest tertiary graduate unemployment
prompt: Name the countries with the highest unemployment rates among people with tertiary (post-secondary) education.

source.name: ILOSTAT / World Bank — Unemployment with advanced education (% of total labor force with advanced education)

disclaimer: Share of the labour force with tertiary education who are unemployed. Reflects labour-market absorption of graduates — a country can have both high graduate unemployment AND low overall unemployment if degrees have expanded faster than skilled jobs.
trivia: In several Middle-East and North-African economies, graduate unemployment has run higher than youth unemployment overall — an unusual pattern that fed into the 2011 Arab Spring protests, many of whose organisers were unemployed university graduates.

title: Largest natural gas pipeline networks
prompt: Name the countries with the longest natural gas pipeline networks (transmission + distribution).

source.name: CIA World Factbook — Pipelines

disclaimer: Combines transmission and distribution gas pipelines; totals are in kilometres.
trivia: The US network alone runs roughly 2.3 million km — about 60 laps around the equator.

title: Largest crude oil pipeline networks
prompt: Name the countries with the longest crude oil pipeline networks.

source.name: CIA World Factbook — Pipelines (crude/oil)

disclaimer: Crude oil trunk pipelines only, in kilometres — excludes refined-product and gas lines.
trivia: Russia's Druzhba ("Friendship") pipeline is the single longest oil pipeline on Earth at ~4,000 km, carrying crude from western Siberia into central Europe.

title: Largest total crude oil importers
prompt: Name the countries that import the most crude oil each year.

source.name: EIA — International crude oil imports

disclaimer: Crude oil imports in millions of barrels per day (mbpd); excludes refined products.
trivia: China surpassed the US as the world's largest crude importer in 2017 and hasn't looked back — it now takes roughly a quarter of all seaborne crude cargoes.

title: Largest total crude oil exporters
prompt: Name the countries that export the most crude oil each year.

source.name: EIA — International crude oil exports

disclaimer: Crude oil exports in millions of barrels per day (mbpd); excludes refined products and NGLs.
trivia: Saudi Arabia and Russia together move roughly a third of the world's crude across borders — and coordinate output through the OPEC+ agreement.

title: Largest natural gas importers
