prompt: Name the countries that import the most natural gas (pipeline + LNG) each year.

source.name: Energy Institute — Statistical Review of World Energy

disclaimer: Combined pipeline and LNG imports in billion cubic metres (bcm) per year.
trivia: Before 2022, Germany was by far Europe's biggest gas importer via pipeline from Russia; the switch to LNG collapsed pipeline volumes and reshuffled the ranking.

title: Highest natural gas consumption
prompt: Name the countries that consume the most natural gas each year.

source.name: Energy Institute — Statistical Review of World Energy

disclaimer: Total natural gas consumption in billion cubic metres (bcm) per year across power, industry and residential use.
trivia: Roughly 40% of US electricity now comes from natural gas — the country burns more gas for power alone than most nations use for all purposes combined.

title: Highest coal consumption
prompt: Name the countries that consume the most coal each year.

source.name: Energy Institute — Statistical Review of World Energy

disclaimer: Total coal consumption measured in exajoules (EJ) of primary energy — includes power, steel and industry.
trivia: Asia now burns roughly 80% of the world's coal; China alone burns more than the rest of the planet combined.

title: Largest total installed power capacity
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total installed electricity generation capacity.

source.name: EIA — International electricity capacity

disclaimer: Total installed nameplate capacity across all fuels (fossil, nuclear, hydro, wind, solar, other) in gigawatts (GW).
trivia: China's total capacity has more than tripled since 2010 — it now adds more solar and wind capacity each year than the entire US fleet.

title: Highest residential electricity prices
prompt: Name the countries where households pay the most for electricity per kilowatt-hour.

source.name: GlobalPetrolPrices — Electricity prices, households

disclaimer: Household tariffs in US dollars per kilowatt-hour (kWh), all-in with taxes and levies.
trivia: European households pay 3-5x what US households pay — a legacy of the 2022 gas crisis, carbon pricing, and heavy grid-fee loadings on residential bills.

title: Largest butter producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most butter (including ghee) by volume.

source.name: FAOSTAT — Crops and livestock products (Butter of cow milk + ghee)

disclaimer: Includes butter of cow milk and clarified butter (ghee) per FAOSTAT. Values in tonnes.
trivia: India alone accounts for roughly half of world butter/ghee output when ghee is included, thanks to the country's massive buffalo milk industry.

title: Largest yogurt markets
prompt: Name the countries with the largest yogurt production/consumption markets by volume.

source.name: Statista / Euromonitor — Yogurt market volume by country

disclaimer: Total market volume in tonnes, combining spoonable, drinking, and Greek-style yogurts. Both production-heavy and consumption-heavy countries appear.
trivia: Turkey — where the word 'yogurt' originates — has the highest per-capita yogurt consumption of any large country, averaging over 35 kg per person annually.

title: Largest ice cream producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most ice cream by volume.

source.name: IDFA / Euromonitor — Global ice cream production volumes

disclaimer: Total ice cream (including gelato and frozen desserts) production in litres. A handful of large populous markets dominate absolute volume.
trivia: New Zealand, though not in the top 10 by volume, leads the world in per-capita ice cream consumption — over 28 litres per person per year.

title: Largest citrus fruits producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most citrus fruit total (oranges, mandarins, lemons, grapefruit, limes).

source.name: FAOSTAT — Citrus fruit total (oranges, tangerines, lemons, limes, grapefruit)

disclaimer: Total citrus production in tonnes across all major citrus categories. Both tropical and subtropical countries can appear in the top ranks.
trivia: China's citrus output has more than tripled since 2000 as mandarin orange cultivation exploded in the southern provinces, particularly Guangxi and Hunan.

title: Largest coffee exporters
prompt: Name the countries that export the most coffee (green bean equivalent).

source.name: International Coffee Organization (ICO) — Total exports by exporting countries

disclaimer: Green coffee bean equivalent (Arabica + Robusta combined), reported in 60-kg bags. Differs from production because some producing countries consume most of their own crop.
trivia: Vietnam supplies roughly 40% of the world's Robusta coffee — the bean used in most espresso blends and instant coffee — despite only starting commercial cultivation in the 1980s.

title: Largest cocoa bean exporters
prompt: Name the countries that export the most cocoa beans by volume.

source.name: International Cocoa Organization (ICCO) — Quarterly Bulletin of Cocoa Statistics

disclaimer: Raw cocoa bean exports in tonnes, not processed cocoa or chocolate products. West Africa dominates global cocoa exports.
trivia: Cote d'Ivoire and Ghana together supply about two-thirds of the world's cocoa beans, but capture less than 6% of the roughly $130 billion global chocolate industry's value.

title: Largest fish and seafood exporters
prompt: Name the countries that export the most fish and seafood by value.

source.name: FAO — State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture (SOFIA), fish trade tables

disclaimer: Total fish and seafood exports by value in USD, including wild-caught and aquaculture, fresh, frozen, and processed forms.
trivia: Norway's salmon farming industry has become so large that a single fjord region can export more salmon in a year than the entire wild Alaskan salmon catch.

title: Most Michelin stars in total
prompt: Name the countries with the most total Michelin Guide stars awarded to their restaurants.

source.name: Michelin Guide — Country totals across guides

disclaimer: Total stars across all Michelin-guide-covered restaurants (3-star counts as 3, 2-star as 2, 1-star as 1). Only countries with a Michelin Guide edition are eligible.
trivia: France and Japan each have more than 30 three-star restaurants, and Tokyo alone consistently has more Michelin stars than any other single city on Earth.

title: Most vegan restaurants per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the most vegan and vegetarian restaurants per capita.

source.name: HappyCow — Global vegan/vegetarian restaurant density index

disclaimer: Vegan and vegetarian restaurants per million residents, based on HappyCow's user-listed directory. Small European and East Asian countries dominate the per-capita ranking.
trivia: Taiwan's high rank comes largely from its Buddhist vegetarian tradition — many temple-adjacent 'sushi' shops have served plant-based food since long before the modern vegan movement.

title: Largest beer exporters
prompt: Name the countries that export the most beer by volume.

source.name: Barth-Haas Group — The Barth Report: Hops and Beer Trade Statistics

disclaimer: Beer exports in hectolitres. Rankings track shipments across borders, so major exporters differ from largest producers.
trivia: Mexico became the world's largest beer exporter in the 2010s largely on the strength of a single brand family — Corona and Modelo — which now outsells all U.S. domestic beers combined.

title: Arctic Council member states
prompt: Name the eight sovereign states that are permanent members of the Arctic Council, whose territory reaches into the Arctic (north of 66.5°N).

source.name: Arctic Council — Member States

disclaimer: The pool is fixed at exactly eight — every member is a permanent seat, so there is no meaningful 'rank' beyond membership. Ranks below are ordered by size of Arctic territory (land area above the Arctic Circle).
trivia: Only one Arctic Council state — Iceland — has no land north of the Arctic Circle on its mainland; the tiny island of Grímsey just barely crosses it.

title: Countries the Equator passes through
prompt: Name the sovereign countries whose land or territorial waters the Equator (0° latitude) passes through.

source.name: Wikipedia — Equator (crossings)

disclaimer: Includes countries where the Equator crosses only maritime territory (Maldives, Kiribati). Ordered west-to-east starting from the Prime Meridian for rank purposes.
trivia: Ecuador is literally named after the Equator, yet the line passes through more of Brazil, DR Congo, and Indonesia than through Ecuador itself.

answers.value: São Tomé and Príncipe (maritime, Gulf of Guinea)

title: Countries the Prime Meridian passes through
prompt: Name the sovereign countries whose land the Prime Meridian (0° longitude) crosses on its way from the North Pole to Antarctica.

source.name: Wikipedia — Prime meridian (Greenwich)

disclaimer: Antarctica is excluded because it is not a sovereign country. Order is north-to-south along the meridian.
trivia: The meridian enters Africa at the coast of Ghana just east of the port city of Tema, then runs almost due north through five countries before crossing the Mediterranean into Europe.

answers.value: Ghana (Tema on the Gulf of Guinea)

title: Countries the Tropic of Cancer crosses
prompt: Name the sovereign countries whose land the Tropic of Cancer (~23.5°N) passes through.

source.name: Wikipedia — Tropic of Cancer

disclaimer: Ordered west-to-east from the International Date Line. Maritime-only crossings (e.g. Cape Verde EEZ, Hawaii's EEZ) are excluded.
trivia: The Tropic of Cancer is drifting south by about 15 metres each year due to Earth's axial precession — it crossed the exact town centre of Chiayi, Taiwan in 1908 and is now noticeably south of it.

title: Countries the Tropic of Capricorn crosses
prompt: Name the sovereign countries whose land the Tropic of Capricorn (~23.5°S) passes through.

source.name: Wikipedia — Tropic of Capricorn

disclaimer: Ordered east-to-west starting from the International Date Line. Includes only land crossings — Pacific and Indian Ocean crossings are omitted.
trivia: There are exactly ten countries the Tropic of Capricorn crosses on land — half of the Cancer count — because the Southern Hemisphere has so much less landmass at that latitude.

answers.value: Brazil (São Paulo state, just south of the city)
Namibia (Kalahari edge, Windhoek is just south)

title: Countries most surrounded by a single neighbour
prompt: Name the sovereign countries whose land border is bounded by only one (or almost only one) other country — the most 'enclosed' nations on Earth.

source.name: Wikipedia — Enclave and exclave (list of enclaved countries)

disclaimer: Rank 1-3 are true enclaves (100% surrounded). Rank 4 onward are 'quasi-enclaves' bordered by one country plus a small coastline. Percentage refers to the share of the land border formed by a single neighbour.
trivia: The Gambia is the most nearly-enclaved country that isn't a microstate — its border with Senegal wraps around it on three sides, following the Gambia River for about 740 km inland from a narrow Atlantic coast.

answers.value: 100% land border with Senegal (short Atlantic coast)
100% land border with Malaysia (short South China Sea coast)
100% land border with Saudi Arabia (rest is Persian Gulf)
100% land border with Germany (Jutland peninsula only)
100% land border with the United Kingdom
100% land border with Spain (rest is Atlantic)
~87% by China (plus Russia and South Korea)

title: Largest single-neighbour border length
prompt: Name the countries with the world's longest continuous land border between two nations (single-pair borders).

source.name: CIA World Factbook — Land boundaries / country comparisons

disclaimer: One entry per bilateral border — countries appear only for their single longest neighbouring border. Length in kilometres of that specific shared border.
trivia: The Canada–United States border is the longest between any two countries on Earth, and if the Alaska–Yukon/BC section is included it stretches for 8,891 km — much of it a straight line along the 49th parallel.

title: Most named waterfalls
prompt: Name the countries that host the greatest number of named, catalogued waterfalls.

source.name: World Waterfall Database / national tourism inventories

disclaimer: Sources use widely different height/flow thresholds, so counts are best-approximation from each country's catalogued inventory. Ordered by absolute number of catalogued named waterfalls.
trivia: Norway's fjord cliffs generate so many high-plunge waterfalls that the country holds eight of the world's twenty tallest, including 818-metre Vinnufossen.

title: Most glacier-covered countries
prompt: Name the countries with the largest total area of glaciers (outside of Antarctica).

source.name: Randolph Glacier Inventory (RGI) v7 / GLIMS

disclaimer: Excludes the Antarctic ice sheet (not a sovereign country). Greenland is credited to Denmark. Values are total glacier area in km².
trivia: Greenland's ice sheet alone accounts for roughly 1.7 million km² — more glacier area than every other non-Antarctic country combined.

title: Countries the Danube flows through
prompt: Name the countries the Danube River flows through or forms a border with, ranked by kilometres of river within their territory.

source.name: International Commission for the Protection of the Danube River / Wikipedia

disclaimer: Length includes stretches where the Danube forms an international border, counted for both bordering countries. Rank 1 has the longest river reach within its territory.
trivia: The Danube passes through more capital cities than any other river on Earth — Vienna, Bratislava, Budapest, and Belgrade all sit on its banks.

title: Countries in the Nile drainage basin
prompt: Name the countries whose territory contributes to the Nile drainage basin (not just the river's main stem).

source.name: Nile Basin Initiative / Wikipedia

disclaimer: Ranked by share of the Nile Basin by area. Includes both the Blue Nile and White Nile tributary systems — many basin countries feed the Nile via tributaries rather than sitting on the main stem.
trivia: Only Egypt and Sudan sit on the Nile's main stem after the confluence at Khartoum — every other basin country contributes via a tributary.

title: Countries in the Amazon drainage basin
prompt: Name the countries whose territory lies within the Amazon River drainage basin (not just the main-stem river).

source.name: Amazon Cooperation Treaty Organization / Wikipedia

disclaimer: Ranked by share of the Amazon Basin by area. Includes all basin countries even where the main-stem river does not enter their territory — Suriname's contribution is via a small headwater catchment, not the main river.
trivia: Only Brazil, Peru, and Colombia contain the Amazon's main stem — the remaining basin countries drain into it through the Napo, Caquetá, Madeira, and other major tributaries.

title: Countries the Mekong flows through
prompt: Name the countries the Mekong River flows through, ranked by kilometres of river within their territory.

source.name: Mekong River Commission / Wikipedia

disclaimer: Includes stretches where the Mekong forms an international border. Rank 1 has the longest river reach within its territory.
trivia: The Mekong falls almost 4,500 metres from its Tibetan headwaters to the South China Sea — most of that drop happens inside China before the river even reaches Laos.

title: Countries the Rhine flows through
prompt: Name the countries the Rhine River flows through or forms a border with, ranked by kilometres of river within their territory.

source.name: International Commission for the Protection of the Rhine / Wikipedia

disclaimer: Includes stretches where the Rhine forms an international border, counted for both bordering countries. Rank 1 has the longest reach within its territory.
trivia: The Rhine's source in the Swiss canton of Graubünden is only about 30 km from the source of three other major rivers — the Rhône, the Ticino (Po), and the Inn (Danube).

title: Largest Antarctic territorial claims
prompt: Name the countries with the largest formal territorial claims on Antarctica.

source.name: Antarctic Treaty Secretariat / Wikipedia

disclaimer: All claims are suspended by Article IV of the Antarctic Treaty and not universally recognised. Rank 1 is the claim covering the largest area. Only seven countries have made formal territorial claims.
trivia: Australia's Antarctic Territory covers about 5.9 million km² — nearly 42% of the entire continent, and larger than Australia's own state of Western Australia.

title: Longest Arctic coastline
prompt: Name the countries with the longest coastline along the Arctic Ocean.

source.name: Arctic Council / Wikipedia

disclaimer: Only eight countries border the Arctic Ocean or its marginal seas. Rank 1 has the longest Arctic coast; figures include major offshore islands.
trivia: Russia and Canada together account for more than two-thirds of the total Arctic coastline, largely because of the archipelagos north of the Siberian and Canadian mainlands.

title: Longest land border
prompt: Name the countries with the longest single international land border with a neighbouring country.

source.name: CIA World Factbook / Wikipedia

disclaimer: Ranks the single longest border each country shares with any one neighbour. Each border is counted once for each of the two bordering countries.
trivia: The Canada–United States border, at nearly 8,900 km including the Alaska–Yukon segment, is the longest between any two countries on Earth.

title: Largest single island within country
prompt: Name the countries containing the largest single island (by area) within their territory.

source.name: Wikipedia — List of islands by area

disclaimer: Rank 1 is the country whose largest single island has the greatest area. Countries are ranked by their single biggest island, not total island area.
trivia: Greenland is the world's largest island — larger than the next three combined — and constitutes the entirety of the Kingdom of Denmark's autonomous Greenlandic territory.

title: Longest river entirely within country
prompt: Name the countries containing the longest river flowing entirely within a single nation's borders (source to mouth inside one country).

source.name: Wikipedia — List of rivers by length

disclaimer: Only rivers whose entire course from source to mouth lies within one country are counted. Rank 1 is the longest such river.
trivia: The Yangtze, at 6,300 km entirely within China, is the longest river on Earth flowing through only one country.

title: Highest average annual wage (OECD)
prompt: Name the countries with the highest average annual wages according to the OECD.

source.name: OECD — Average Wages database

disclaimer: Values are in constant 2023 USD at purchasing power parity, covering only OECD member countries.
trivia: Iceland and Luxembourg regularly swap places at the top of this list; both are small economies with unusually high compensation floors.

title: Highest minimum wage per hour
prompt: Name the countries with the highest statutory minimum wage per hour in nominal USD.

source.name: OECD — Real minimum wages / national statutes

disclaimer: Nominal USD converted at market exchange rates, not PPP; countries without a statutory national minimum wage (e.g. some Nordic states) are excluded.

title: Longest statutory paid vacation
prompt: Name the countries with the most statutory paid vacation days per year (excluding public holidays).

source.name: Mercer — Worldwide Benefit and Employment Guidelines / ILO

disclaimer: Refers to minimum statutory annual leave entitlement for a full-time employee; public holidays are counted separately in another question.
trivia: France's five-week entitlement dates to 1982 and was one of the flagship reforms of the Mitterrand government.

title: Longest paid parental leave (OECD)
prompt: Name the countries with the longest total paid parental and maternity leave available to mothers.

source.name: OECD Family Database — PF2.1 Parental leave systems

disclaimer: Total weeks of paid leave reserved for or shared with mothers, combining maternity and parental leave; excludes unpaid extensions.
trivia: Estonia's leave is the OECD's longest at over 80 weeks and is compensated at 100 percent of previous earnings for most of that period.

title: Highest union membership rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of employees who are members of a trade union.

source.name: OECD/AIAS ICTWSS database — Trade union density

disclaimer: Trade union density is the number of union members divided by total wage and salary earners; Ghent-system countries (unions administer unemployment insurance) tend to score highest.
trivia: The four highest-density countries all operate Ghent-style unemployment insurance, which gives workers a direct financial reason to join a union.

title: Highest gender pay gap (OECD)
prompt: Name the OECD countries with the largest gender wage gap for full-time employees.

source.name: OECD — Gender wage gap indicator

disclaimer: Measured as the difference between median earnings of men and women relative to median earnings of men, for full-time employees; not adjusted for occupation or seniority.
trivia: South Korea has had the widest gender wage gap in the OECD every year since the indicator was first published in 2000.

title: Highest labor productivity per hour
prompt: Name the countries with the highest GDP per hour worked (labor productivity).

source.name: OECD — GDP per hour worked

disclaimer: GDP per hour worked measured in constant 2015 USD at purchasing power parity; only OECD member countries are included.
trivia: Ireland's figure is heavily inflated by multinational tax structuring, which is why economists often quote a 'modified' Irish productivity number about a third lower.

title: Most public holidays per year
prompt: Name the countries with the most nationally recognized public holidays each year.

source.name: Mercer / ILO — Public Holidays Around the World

disclaimer: Counts nationally observed public holidays only; regional or religious holidays observed in only part of a country are excluded, and ties are broken alphabetically.
trivia: Nepal's public-holiday count reflects the country's mix of Hindu, Buddhist, and Islamic observances alongside secular commemorations, giving it one of the most religiously plural holiday calendars in the world.

title: Highest workplace engagement (Gallup)
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of employees classified as engaged at work in the Gallup State of the Global Workplace survey.

source.name: Gallup — State of the Global Workplace

disclaimer: Percent of employees who are 'engaged' in Gallup's definition (psychologically committed to and enthusiastic about their work); not the same as 'satisfied.'
trivia: The global average engagement rate is only about 23 percent, meaning even the top-ranked countries have a majority of employees who are merely 'not engaged.'

title: Countries where German is official or working
prompt: Name the countries where German is a de jure official or nationally recognized working language.

source.name: Ethnologue / national constitutions (Germany, Austria, Switzerland, Liechtenstein, Luxembourg, Belgium, Italy — South Tyrol)

disclaimer: Ranked by German-speaking population. Includes countries where German is an official national language (e.g. constitutional) or a co-official regional language. Namibia recognized German as a national language until 1990 and it remains widely spoken but is no longer official.
trivia: Luxembourg has three official languages (Luxembourgish, French, German), with German dominating the print press and the school system's early years.

title: Countries where Russian is official
prompt: Name the countries where Russian is a de jure official or co-official language at the national level.

source.name: National constitutions / Ethnologue

disclaimer: Includes countries where Russian is nationally official or co-official. Excludes places where Russian is only regionally official (e.g. Gagauzia, Transnistria). Kazakhstan lists Russian as an official 'language of interethnic communication' alongside Kazakh as state language.
trivia: Kyrgyzstan's constitution names Kyrgyz as the state language but explicitly makes Russian an official language — a rarity among post-Soviet republics.

title: Countries where Chinese is official
prompt: Name the countries or territories where a variety of Chinese (Mandarin, Cantonese, etc.) is a de jure official language.

source.name: National constitutions / Ethnologue

disclaimer: Includes sovereign states and Special Administrative Regions where Chinese has official status. Ranked by Chinese-speaking population. Only five entities globally have Chinese as an official language.
trivia: Singapore's four official languages are English, Malay, Mandarin, and Tamil — Malay is the national language but English is the language of administration.

title: Countries where a Turkic language is dominant
prompt: Name the countries where a Turkic language (Turkish, Azerbaijani, Kazakh, etc.) is the dominant national language.

source.name: Ethnologue — Turkic language family

disclaimer: Includes independent states whose state language belongs to the Turkic family. Ranked by number of native speakers of the state Turkic language.
trivia: Turkey, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan formed the Organization of Turkic States, promoting linguistic and cultural ties across the Turkic world.

title: Countries using Cyrillic script officially
prompt: Name the countries whose official state language is written in Cyrillic script.

source.name: National constitutions / Unicode CLDR

disclaimer: Includes sovereign states where at least one official state language uses Cyrillic as its primary script. Ranked by population of the country. Kazakhstan is transitioning Kazakh to Latin script (target 2031) but currently uses Cyrillic officially.
trivia: Bulgaria's accession to the EU in 2007 made Cyrillic the third official script of the European Union, alongside Latin and Greek.

title: Countries using Arabic script officially
prompt: Name the countries whose official state language is written primarily in Arabic script.

source.name: National constitutions / Ethnologue

disclaimer: Includes states where the constitutional national language is written in Arabic script (Arabic, Persian, Urdu, Pashto, Dari). Ranked by country population. Excludes states that recognize Arabic only regionally.
trivia: Pakistan's Urdu shares nearly identical grammar with India's Hindi, but the two are written in different scripts (Perso-Arabic vs Devanagari), making them mutually intelligible spoken but not written.

title: Countries with sign language officially recognized
prompt: Name the countries that have officially recognized a national sign language in law or constitution.

source.name: World Federation of the Deaf — Sign Language Recognition

disclaimer: Includes countries with statutory or constitutional recognition of at least one national sign language. Ranked chronologically by year of first recognition (rank 1 = earliest).
trivia: Uganda was the first country in the world to enshrine sign language recognition directly in its constitution, doing so in 1995 as part of its post-conflict rewriting of national law.

title: Countries with the most endangered languages
prompt: Name the countries with the most endangered languages listed in the UNESCO Atlas of the World's Languages in Danger.

source.name: UNESCO Atlas of the World's Languages in Danger
source.asOf: UNESCO Atlas 3rd edition (2010, most recent aggregate)

disclaimer: Counts distinct languages classified as vulnerable, definitely endangered, severely endangered, critically endangered, or extinct since 1950 within each country's borders. Countries with high linguistic diversity dominate.
trivia: India's endangered languages include hundreds of tribal and Himalayan tongues, and its highest concentration of at-risk languages is in the northeastern states bordering Myanmar and China.
asOfDate: UNESCO Atlas 3rd edition (2010, most recent aggregate)

title: Countries where a Romance language is dominant
prompt: Name the countries where a Romance language (Spanish, Portuguese, French, Italian, Romanian) is the dominant national language, ranked by population.

source.name: Ethnologue — Romance language family

disclaimer: Ranked by country population. Includes sovereign states where a Romance language is the sole or primary national/state language. Excludes countries where a Romance language is only co-official alongside a non-Romance national language.
trivia: Brazil has more Portuguese speakers than Portugal, Angola, and Mozambique combined — making it the world's largest lusophone country by a factor of nearly 20.

title: Countries where a Slavic language is dominant
prompt: Name the countries where a Slavic language (Russian, Polish, Ukrainian, Serbo-Croatian, Czech, etc.) is the dominant national language, ranked by population.

source.name: Ethnologue — Slavic language family

disclaimer: Ranked by country population. Includes sovereign states where a Slavic language is the sole or primary state language. Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Croatia, and Montenegro share the same underlying South Slavic dialect continuum but are listed separately per their own constitutional naming.
trivia: Russian is the most-spoken Slavic language by a wide margin; every other Slavic-language country combined still has fewer native speakers than Russia alone.

title: Largest paper & paperboard producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most paper and paperboard.

source.name: FAO — Forestry Production and Trade (FAOSTAT)

disclaimer: Total paper and paperboard production in metric tonnes, covering newsprint, printing/writing, packaging and other paper grades combined.
trivia: Paper production has shifted markedly east — the top producer alone makes more paper than North America and Europe combined, driven largely by e-commerce packaging demand.

title: Largest plastics producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most plastic resins and materials.

source.name: Plastics Europe — Plastics: The Facts
source.asOf: 2022 production year (Plastics Europe / regional plastic associations)

disclaimer: Country/region share of global plastic materials (thermoplastics, thermosets and elastomers) production. Regional aggregates split proportionally across producing countries where available.
trivia: Just one country now accounts for roughly a third of global plastic output — more than all of Europe and North America combined.
asOfDate: 2022 production year (Plastics Europe / regional plastic associations)

title: Largest tire producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most tires by units.

source.name: Tyre Industry Research / European Rubber Journal

disclaimer: Total tire production (passenger, truck, off-road) in units, by country where the tires are actually manufactured. Excludes imports.
trivia: Southeast Asia has become a huge tire manufacturing hub as rubber-tree-friendly climates converge with foreign brand assembly investment.

title: Largest fertilizer producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most fertilizer (nitrogen, phosphate, and potash combined).

source.name: IFA — International Fertilizer Association / FAOSTAT

disclaimer: Total fertilizer output in tonnes of nutrient (N + P2O5 + K2O), summing nitrogenous, phosphate and potash production. Domestic mining/refining, not consumption.
trivia: Fertilizer production is highly geographic — potash is dominated by countries with subsurface salt deposits, while nitrogen production tracks natural gas supply.

title: Largest glass producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most flat and container glass.

source.name: Glass Global / U.S. Geological Survey — Industrial Minerals

disclaimer: Combined flat glass (float, sheet) and container glass output measured in millions of tonnes. Excludes fiberglass and specialty glass.
trivia: Container glass and flat glass output correlate with construction booms — the top producer alone accounts for over half of world flat glass capacity.

title: Largest footwear producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most pairs of footwear.

source.name: World Footwear Yearbook (APICCAPS)

disclaimer: Total footwear output in pairs, all categories (leather, synthetic, athletic, casual). Country of manufacture, not brand HQ.
trivia: The top producer accounts for roughly 55% of world footwear output, and along with the runner-up makes up over two-thirds of every shoe on Earth.

title: Largest wind turbine manufacturers by country of HQ
prompt: Name the countries whose companies produced the most wind turbine capacity globally.

source.name: BloombergNEF / Wood Mackenzie — Global Wind Turbine OEM Market Share

disclaimer: Global installed wind capacity attributed to OEMs, grouped by the country of the OEM's headquarters.
trivia: For the first time in the industry's history, more than 60% of world wind capacity now comes from OEMs headquartered in a single country — a dramatic reversal from a decade ago when Denmark and Germany led.

title: Largest solar panel producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most solar photovoltaic (PV) modules.

source.name: IEA — Special Report on Solar PV Global Supply Chains

disclaimer: Country share of global solar PV module manufacturing capacity, measured in gigawatts of annual output. Country of manufacture, not brand HQ.
trivia: One country now controls more than 80% of every stage in the PV supply chain — polysilicon, wafers, cells, and modules — a level of dominance the IEA calls unprecedented in modern energy manufacturing.

title: Largest EV battery producers
prompt: Name the countries whose companies produce the most electric vehicle battery capacity.

source.name: SNE Research / BloombergNEF — Global EV Battery Rankings
source.asOf: 2023 deployed EV battery capacity by manufacturer HQ (SNE Research)

disclaimer: Share of global EV battery capacity deployed by manufacturers, grouped by country of HQ. Includes lithium-ion cells for BEVs and PHEVs. Actual production may occur in multiple countries.
trivia: The two leading nations' companies together supply more than 90% of the world's EV batteries — the top firm alone provides roughly 4 in every 10 EV batteries globally.
asOfDate: 2023 deployed EV battery capacity by manufacturer HQ (SNE Research)

title: Largest food processing sectors by value
prompt: Name the countries with the largest food processing industry output by dollar value.

source.name: UNIDO — Industrial Statistics / OECD Food & Agriculture

disclaimer: Gross output of the food, beverage and tobacco processing sector (ISIC divisions 10-12) in USD billions. Excludes primary agriculture and food retail.
trivia: Food processing is one of the few manufacturing sectors where the US actually leads on absolute value, thanks to its scale in meatpacking, dairy, and packaged foods.

title: Most fighter/interceptor aircraft
prompt: Name the countries with the largest fleets of fighter and interceptor aircraft in active military service.

source.name: IISS Military Balance / Flight Global World Air Forces

disclaimer: Counts dedicated fighter and multirole strike-fighter airframes only. Trainers, attack helicopters, and dedicated bombers are excluded. Active in-service inventory, not stored reserves.
trivia: The F-35 alone accounts for over 1,000 airframes worldwide, with more than 700 in US service across three military branches.

title: Most nuclear-powered submarines
prompt: Name the countries operating the largest fleets of nuclear-powered submarines (all types).

source.name: IISS Military Balance / Nuclear Threat Initiative

disclaimer: Includes SSNs (attack), SSBNs (ballistic missile), and SSGNs (cruise missile) — any submarine with a nuclear reactor as its primary propulsion. Diesel-electric and air-independent-propulsion boats are excluded. Only six nations operate nuclear submarines.
trivia: The US and Russia together operate about 80% of the world's nuclear submarines, and only six countries have ever fielded them.

title: Most non-nuclear submarines
prompt: Name the countries with the largest fleets of diesel-electric or air-independent-propulsion (non-nuclear) submarines.

source.name: IISS Military Balance / Global Firepower submarine tables

disclaimer: Conventional submarines only — diesel-electric, AIP, and stirling-engine boats. Nuclear-powered submarines are excluded. Midget submarines under 150 tons are also excluded.
trivia: North Korea's submarine count is inflated by dozens of ageing Romeo-class and Sang-O midget boats, most useful only in coastal roles.

title: Most ballistic missile submarines (SSBNs)
prompt: Name the countries operating the largest fleets of nuclear-armed ballistic missile submarines.

source.name: Federation of American Scientists / Nuclear Threat Initiative

disclaimer: Only counts strategic ballistic missile submarines (SSBNs) — those carrying submarine-launched ballistic missiles as strategic nuclear deterrents. Cruise missile subs (SSGNs) and attack subs (SSNs) are excluded.
trivia: The five permanent UN Security Council members plus India are the only countries operating strategic submarines — all six are declared or de-facto nuclear powers.

title: Most military UAVs/drones in service
prompt: Name the countries operating the largest fleets of military unmanned aerial vehicles (drones).

source.name: IISS Military Balance / Bard Center for Drone Studies estimates

disclaimer: Includes armed and unarmed military UAVs of tactical class and above, based on published inventories and export tracking. Small commercial-derived quadcopters used in Ukraine-Russia are excluded from these counts. Numbers are approximate — many programs are classified.
trivia: Turkey's Bayraktar TB2 drone has been exported to nearly 30 countries and became famous during the Nagorno-Karabakh and Ukraine conflicts.

title: Most land-based artillery pieces
prompt: Name the countries with the largest land-based artillery arsenals (towed, self-propelled, and rocket artillery combined).

source.name: Global Firepower / IISS Military Balance

disclaimer: Combines towed artillery, self-propelled artillery, and multiple-launch rocket systems. Mortars are excluded. Reserve and stored inventory partially included when authoritative sources report it.
trivia: North Korea's artillery is heavily concentrated along the DMZ, with thousands of tubes reportedly ranged on Seoul from hardened positions.

title: Most military helicopters
prompt: Name the countries with the largest fleets of military helicopters (all roles: attack, transport, utility).

source.name: Flight Global World Air Forces / IISS Military Balance

disclaimer: Includes attack, transport, utility, and search-and-rescue helicopters in active military service. Civilian and coast-guard-only fleets are excluded.
trivia: The US Army alone operates more helicopters than any other country's entire armed forces — over 4,000, including some 700 AH-64 Apaches.

title: Top arms-manufacturing countries (SIPRI)
prompt: Name the countries whose defence companies collectively sold the most arms globally, per the SIPRI Top 100 Arms Producers list.

source.name: SIPRI Top 100 Arms-Producing Companies

disclaimer: Ranked by combined arms-related revenue of each country's companies on the SIPRI Top 100 list. Chinese totals are SIPRI estimates due to reporting opacity.
trivia: US-headquartered companies dominate the SIPRI Top 100 with over half of total revenue — Lockheed Martin alone had more arms revenue than the entire UK defence industry.

title: Highest per-capita defense spending
prompt: Name the countries that spend the most on their military per resident (per capita).

source.name: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database (per-capita computed vs UN population)

disclaimer: Annual defense budget divided by total population. Excludes microstates without independent armed forces (Vatican, Monaco, Liechtenstein).
trivia: Israel's high per-capita defense spending includes substantial US military aid — roughly $3.8 billion annually — funneled into its budget.

title: Longest mandatory military service
prompt: Name the countries with the longest duration of mandatory military conscription for eligible citizens.

source.name: CIA World Factbook / War Resisters' International conscription database

disclaimer: Represents baseline compulsory service for male citizens. Officer tracks, alternative civilian service, and reserve-training terms are excluded. Ranked by standard active-duty months required.
trivia: South Korea's ~18-month term is one reason K-pop stars like BTS members individually enlist — no automatic exemption for entertainers exists.

title: Largest zinc producers
prompt: Name the countries that mine the most zinc by contained metal content.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Zinc

disclaimer: Mine production of zinc concentrate, expressed as contained metal in thousand metric tonnes.
trivia: About half of all zinc mined is used for galvanizing steel to protect it from corrosion.

title: Largest lead producers
prompt: Name the countries that mine the most lead by contained metal content.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Lead

disclaimer: Mine production of lead in concentrate, expressed as contained metal in thousand metric tonnes.
trivia: Roughly 85% of all lead consumed today is used to make lead-acid batteries for vehicles and backup power.

title: Largest tin producers
prompt: Name the countries that mine the most tin by contained metal content.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Tin

disclaimer: Mine production of tin in concentrate, expressed as contained metal in thousand metric tonnes.
trivia: Tin's largest single use is as solder in electronics; the transition from leaded solder drove a decade-long surge in tin demand.

title: Largest silver producers
prompt: Name the countries that mine the most silver by contained metal content.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Silver

disclaimer: Mine production of silver in metric tonnes.
trivia: Most silver comes as a by-product of lead, zinc, copper, or gold mining rather than from primary silver mines.

title: Largest platinum producers
prompt: Name the countries that mine the most platinum.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Platinum-Group Metals

disclaimer: Mine production of platinum in kilograms of contained metal.
trivia: The Bushveld Complex in South Africa contains the world's largest known reserves of platinum-group metals — over 70% of the global total.

title: Largest palladium producers
prompt: Name the countries that mine the most palladium.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Platinum-Group Metals

disclaimer: Mine production of palladium in kilograms of contained metal.
trivia: Palladium prices surged past gold in the late 2010s, driven by tightening auto-emissions rules that increased catalyst loadings in gasoline vehicles.

title: Largest rare earth producers
prompt: Name the countries that mine the most rare earth elements (REO content).

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Rare Earths

disclaimer: Mine production of rare earth oxide (REO) equivalent, in metric tonnes.
trivia: China dominates not just mining but also the refining stage — over 85% of separated rare earth oxide capacity sits inside China.

title: Largest bauxite producers
prompt: Name the countries that mine the most bauxite (the ore for aluminum).

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Bauxite and Alumina

disclaimer: Mine production of bauxite in million metric tonnes.
trivia: Guinea sits on the world's largest bauxite reserves and has become the leading supplier of ore feeding China's alumina refineries.

title: Largest phosphate rock producers
prompt: Name the countries that mine the most phosphate rock.

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Phosphate Rock

disclaimer: Mine production of phosphate rock in million metric tonnes.
trivia: Morocco (including Western Sahara) is estimated to hold over 70% of the world's phosphate rock reserves — a strategic lever for global agriculture.

title: Largest potash producers
prompt: Name the countries that produce the most potash (K2O equivalent).

source.name: USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries — Potash

disclaimer: Production expressed as K2O equivalent in million metric tonnes.
trivia: Canada's Saskatchewan basin holds about half of the world's proven potash reserves and hosts the largest potash mine on earth.

title: Largest tropical forest cover
prompt: Name the countries with the greatest area of tropical rainforest cover.

source.name: Global Forest Watch / World Resources Institute — Tropical primary forest extent

disclaimer: Ranks by area of humid tropical primary forest, not total forest of any kind. Excludes boreal and temperate forest.
trivia: The Amazon Basin holds about 40% of the world's remaining tropical rainforest, and roughly two-thirds of it lies within a single country's borders.

title: Largest boreal forest (taiga) cover
prompt: Name the countries with the greatest area of boreal forest (taiga).

source.name: FAO Global Forest Resources Assessment — Boreal domain

disclaimer: Boreal forest ranges through the sub-Arctic across only a handful of countries. The pool of qualifying countries is small — most of the ranking is a two-horse race with a long tail.
trivia: The taiga is Earth's largest terrestrial biome, and Russia's share alone accounts for roughly one-fifth of all the forest on the planet.

title: Country containing the tallest mountain within its borders
prompt: Name the countries whose highest peak within their national borders is the tallest.

source.name: USGS / Peakbagger — Country high points

disclaimer: Ranks each country by the elevation of its highest peak. Shared border peaks count for both countries (e.g., Everest is on the Nepal-China border).
trivia: Nepal and China share Everest at 8,849 m, and Pakistan holds the world's second-highest at K2 despite having a smaller Himalayan share than either neighbour.

title: Country containing the deepest lake
prompt: Name the countries whose territory contains a lake of extraordinary depth.

source.name: USGS / International Lake Environment Committee — Lake bathymetry

disclaimer: Ranks by the maximum depth of the deepest natural lake fully or partially within a country. Shared lakes count for each bordering country.
trivia: Lake Baikal in Russia is the deepest lake on Earth at 1,642 m and also the world's oldest lake at over 25 million years old.

title: Country containing the largest river by discharge
prompt: Name the countries whose territory contains a river with the greatest average freshwater discharge to the sea.

source.name: USGS / World Meteorological Organization — River discharge

disclaimer: Ranks by the mean annual discharge of the single largest river system passing through each country. Shared river basins count for each country the river flows through.
trivia: The Amazon discharges more water than the next seven largest rivers combined, and about 20% of all freshwater entering the world's oceans comes from its mouth.

title: Largest Ramsar wetlands by area
prompt: Name the countries with the greatest total area of internationally designated Ramsar wetlands.

source.name: Ramsar Convention Secretariat — Ramsar Sites Information Service

disclaimer: Only counts wetlands officially designated under the 1971 Ramsar Convention. Real wetland extent may be larger; only designated sites are tallied.
trivia: Bolivia's Llanos de Moxos alone covers 6.9 Mha, making it the single largest Ramsar site in the world.

title: Largest peatlands by area
prompt: Name the countries with the greatest area of peatlands.

source.name: UN Environment Programme — Global Peatlands Assessment

disclaimer: Ranks by total mapped peatland area including both active and drained peatlands. Peatlands store more carbon than all the world's forests combined despite covering only 3% of land area.
trivia: The Cuvette Centrale peatlands of the Congo Basin, discovered in 2017, store about 30 billion tonnes of carbon — three years of global fossil-fuel emissions.

title: Country containing the longest cave system
prompt: Name the countries whose territory contains the longest surveyed cave systems.

source.name: National Speleological Society — World's longest caves list

disclaimer: Ranks by the total surveyed passage length of the single longest cave within each country. New surveys can and do change these rankings from year to year.
trivia: Mammoth Cave in Kentucky is more than twice as long as the second-longest cave on Earth, with over 686 km of mapped passages.

title: Country hosting the driest desert
prompt: Name the countries whose territory contains the driest (lowest annual precipitation) desert or hyper-arid zones.

source.name: NASA Earth Observatory / WMO — Global aridity index

disclaimer: Ranks by the lowest recorded long-term annual precipitation of an arid region within each country. Some parts of the Atacama have gone decades without measurable rainfall.
trivia: Parts of Chile's Atacama Desert have gone over 400 years without significant rain, and NASA uses it as a Mars analog for testing rovers.

title: Largest ice cap or glacier area
prompt: Name the countries with the greatest area of glaciers and ice caps within their territory.

source.name: USGS / Randolph Glacier Inventory — Global glacier area

disclaimer: Excludes Antarctica (not a country). Greenland is listed separately although it is part of the Kingdom of Denmark. Includes both mountain glaciers and continental ice sheets.
trivia: Greenland's ice sheet holds enough water to raise global sea levels by roughly 7 meters if it melted completely.

title: Highest EIU Democracy Index score
prompt: Name the countries with the highest Democracy Index scores according to the Economist Intelligence Unit.

source.name: Economist Intelligence Unit — Democracy Index 2023

disclaimer: Composite score (0-10) across electoral process, civil liberties, political participation, political culture, and functioning of government. Higher is better.
trivia: The EIU classifies only about 24 countries as 'full democracies' — the rest of the top 20 fall into that group, with Norway consistently ranking first since 2010.

title: Lowest EIU Democracy Index score
prompt: Name the countries with the lowest Democracy Index scores (the most authoritarian regimes) according to the Economist Intelligence Unit.

source.name: Economist Intelligence Unit — Democracy Index 2023

disclaimer: Composite score (0-10). Rank 1 here is the lowest scorer (most authoritarian). All entries fall in the EIU's 'authoritarian regime' category.
trivia: Afghanistan replaced Myanmar at the bottom of the ranking following the Taliban's 2021 takeover and subsequent dismantling of political institutions.

title: Highest V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index
prompt: Name the countries with the highest scores on the V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index.

source.name: V-Dem Institute — Democracy Report 2024

disclaimer: Score is 0-1, combining electoral democracy with liberal-democratic institutions (rule of law, checks on executive, minority rights). Higher is better.
trivia: V-Dem's methodology relies on ratings from over 4,000 country experts worldwide — Denmark's near-perfect score reflects consensus across independent judiciary, media, and civil liberties measures.

title: Most successful coups d'état since 1950
prompt: Name the countries that have experienced the most successful coups d'état since 1950.

source.name: Cline Center Coup D'état Project (University of Illinois)

disclaimer: Counts only successful coups (where perpetrators held power for at least 7 days). Excludes attempted-but-failed coups, autogolpes counted per event.
trivia: Bolivia's political instability produced more successful coups than any other Latin American country — including the 'Cocaine Coup' of 1980 led by Luis Garcia Meza.

title: Most coup attempts since 1950
prompt: Name the countries that have experienced the most coup attempts (successful and failed combined) since 1950.

source.name: Powell & Thyne — Global Instances of Coups Dataset (Univ. of Kentucky)

disclaimer: Includes both successful and failed coup attempts. A coup is defined as an illegal and overt attempt by the military or other elites to unseat the sitting executive.
trivia: Sudan has seen more coup attempts than any other country in modern history, with instability continuing through the 2019 revolution and the 2021 military takeover.

title: Highest voter registration rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest voter registration rate (registered voters as a share of the voting-age population).

source.name: International IDEA — Voter Turnout Database

disclaimer: Registered voters divided by voting-age population, based on the most recent parliamentary or presidential election. Rates can exceed 100% due to census lag, dual citizenship, or non-purged rolls.
trivia: Rwanda's near-universal registration reflects a highly centralized administration where enrollment is automatic upon reaching voting age, a system also used in several other African democracies.

title: Most 'Not Free' countries — worst Freedom House score
prompt: Name the countries with the worst (lowest) aggregate Freedom in the World score from Freedom House.

source.name: Freedom House — Freedom in the World 2024

disclaimer: Aggregate score 0-100 combining political rights (0-40) and civil liberties (0-60). Rank 1 here is the lowest scorer (least free).
trivia: Tibet has ranked as one of the least free territories every year since Freedom House began scoring it — its score of 0 has been shared only with South Sudan and Syria in recent editions.

title: Longest-ruling single political party (continuous)
prompt: Name the countries whose currently-ruling political party has held uninterrupted executive power the longest.

source.name: Wikipedia (aggregating national election records) — List of longest-ruling political parties

disclaimer: Continuous years the current ruling party has held executive power as of 2024. Excludes personal dictatorships without a formal party structure. Ties broken by founding date.
trivia: Syria's Ba'ath Party had ruled continuously since 1963 until the Assad government collapsed on 8 December 2024, ending one of the longest single-party runs of the modern era.

title: Highest V-Dem Political Violence Index
prompt: Name the countries with the highest levels of political violence according to V-Dem's index of state-perpetrated and non-state political violence.

source.name: V-Dem Institute — Political Violence indicators

disclaimer: Composite of V-Dem indicators including physical violence index (inverted) and civil war intensity. Higher score = more political violence.
trivia: Myanmar's civil conflict since the 2021 coup has produced one of the sharpest year-over-year declines in the V-Dem physical integrity index ever recorded.

title: Most political prisoners (Amnesty / civil society estimates)
prompt: Name the countries reported to hold the most political prisoners according to Amnesty International and allied human rights organizations.

source.name: Amnesty International — Annual Report 2023/24 and country submissions

disclaimer: Estimates vary widely by definition (prisoners of conscience vs. all political detainees). Figures rounded to nearest reported thousand where available.
trivia: China's estimated total is driven mostly by mass detention of Uyghurs in Xinjiang — independent tribunals put the figure at over 1 million, though Beijing rejects the count.

title: Worst air pollution (highest PM2.5)
prompt: Name the countries with the worst annual average PM2.5 air pollution.

source.name: IQAir — World Air Quality Report

disclaimer: Ranked by annual mean PM2.5 (micrograms per cubic metre). WHO's 2021 guideline is 5 ug/m3.
trivia: Bangladesh's annual PM2.5 average was over 15x the WHO guideline in 2023, largely driven by winter smog in Dhaka combined with cross-border transport from northern India.

title: Cleanest air (lowest PM2.5)
prompt: Name the countries with the lowest annual average PM2.5 air pollution.

source.name: IQAir — World Air Quality Report

disclaimer: Ranked by annual mean PM2.5 (ug/m3), lowest first. Only countries with monitoring station coverage in the IQAir report are ranked.
trivia: French Polynesia and a few other Pacific/Southern Ocean territories often edge out even Finland; among the world's 10 cleanest-air jurisdictions, only Iceland and New Zealand had PM2.5 within WHO's 5 ug/m3 guideline in 2023.

title: Most plastic waste per capita
prompt: Name the countries generating the most plastic waste per person each year.

source.name: Our World in Data — Plastic pollution (Jambeck et al.)

disclaimer: Kilograms of plastic waste generated per person per year (all sources — packaging, textiles, construction, etc.), regardless of how it's managed.
trivia: Kuwait tops the OWID per-capita plastic waste ranking mostly because of extremely high bottled-water consumption and single-use packaging in a hot climate.

title: Most plastic dumped in oceans
prompt: Name the countries responsible for the largest share of plastic waste entering the world's oceans.

source.name: Our World in Data — Ocean plastics (Meijer et al. 2021)

disclaimer: Measured as tonnes of mismanaged plastic emitted to the ocean via rivers, coastlines, and drift — not total plastic produced. Small coastal states with heavy river outflow rank higher than raw production alone would suggest.
trivia: Just two rivers — the Pasig in the Philippines and the Klang in Malaysia — account for a huge share of the Philippines' ocean plastic total; the Philippines alone emits about a third of all plastic entering the sea globally.

title: Highest per-capita e-waste generation
prompt: Name the countries generating the most electronic waste per person each year.

source.name: UN Global E-waste Monitor (UNITAR/ITU)

disclaimer: Kilograms of e-waste generated per capita per year — includes discarded phones, laptops, appliances, batteries, PV panels, and toys.
trivia: Norway and the UK top the list mainly because of high household appliance ownership and rapid replacement cycles; e-waste is growing 5x faster than documented recycling worldwide.

title: Highest access to safe drinking water
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of population using safely managed drinking water services.

source.name: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP)

disclaimer: Percentage of population using an improved water source located on premises, available when needed, and free of contamination. Many high-income countries tie at ~100%; the JMP suppresses decimals above 99%.
trivia: Only about three-quarters of the world's population had safely managed drinking water in 2022 — the remaining 2.2 billion people either share sources, walk to collect water, or drink from unsafe supplies.

title: Highest access to improved sanitation
prompt: Name the countries with the highest share of population using safely managed sanitation services.

source.name: WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme (JMP)

disclaimer: Share of population using an improved sanitation facility not shared with other households, where excreta are safely disposed of or treated off-site. Many wealthy countries tie at ~99-100%.
trivia: About 3.5 billion people globally still lacked safely managed sanitation in 2022 — including 419 million who practise open defecation, concentrated in a handful of sub-Saharan African and South Asian countries.

disclaimer: Counts active and historic lighthouses recorded in the ARLHS World List of Lights; small unmanned navigation lights and buoys are excluded.

title: Countries with the largest shopping malls
prompt: Name the countries home to the world's largest shopping malls by gross leasable area (single mall).

source.name: Wikipedia — List of largest shopping malls

disclaimer: Ranked by gross leasable area (GLA) of a single country's largest mall; airport retail and multi-mall complexes are excluded.
trivia: Iran's Iran Mall is the largest shopping mall in the world by total area (over 1.95 million m²), narrowly ahead of China's New South China Mall.

answers.value: New South China Mall — 892,000 m² GLA
SM Tianjin (SM Mall of Asia complex) — 600,000 m² GLA
Mall of Arabia Jeddah — 261,000 m² GLA

title: Countries with the most historical bridges (pre-1900)
prompt: Which countries have the most surviving historical bridges built before 1900 (Roman, medieval, and pre-industrial bridges)?

source.name: Wikipedia — Lists of historic bridges by country

disclaimer: Counts stone, brick, or timber bridges still in service or preserved with construction dates before 1900; heavily rebuilt bridges retaining original substructure are included.
trivia: Italy has more surviving Roman-era bridges in continuous use than any other country, including the 2,000-year-old Ponte di Tiberio in Rimini.

title: Highest asthma prevalence
prompt: Name the countries with the highest age-standardised prevalence of asthma across all ages.

source.name: IHME — Global Burden of Disease (GBD)

disclaimer: Age-standardised prevalence per 100,000 population, all ages. English-speaking and high-income countries dominate partly because of stronger diagnostic capture.
trivia: The ISAAC childhood asthma surveys first flagged the anglophone-country clustering in the 1990s; higher indoor allergen exposure and diagnostic sensitivity both play a role.

title: Highest cardiovascular disease death rate
prompt: Name the countries with the highest age-standardised mortality rate from cardiovascular disease.

source.name: WHO — Global Health Estimates

disclaimer: Age-standardised deaths per 100,000, from ischaemic heart disease + stroke + other CVD. Rates cluster heavily in post-Soviet states and Central Asia.
trivia: Cardiovascular disease is the single biggest cause of death globally; a heavy salt/alcohol/tobacco burden and weaker acute cardiac care drive the eastern-European lead.

title: Lowest stroke death rate
prompt: Name the countries with the lowest age-standardised stroke mortality rate.

source.name: IHME — Global Burden of Disease (GBD)

disclaimer: Age-standardised stroke deaths per 100,000. Rank 1 = lowest. Countries with populations under 500,000 are excluded to reduce statistical noise.
trivia: Switzerland and France benefit from dense stroke-unit networks; both have door-to-needle times for thrombolysis under 40 minutes at most tertiary centres.

title: Highest dental care spending per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita spending on dental care.

source.name: OECD Health at a Glance — Dental Expenditure

disclaimer: Total (public + private out-of-pocket) dental expenditure per capita in USD PPP. OECD countries only; smaller markets not sampled by OECD are excluded.
trivia: Dental spending is one of the most privately-financed categories of health care — over 75% out-of-pocket even in high-spending countries like Switzerland and Germany.

title: Highest hearing loss prevalence
prompt: Name the countries with the highest age-standardised prevalence of moderate or greater hearing loss.

source.name: IHME — Global Burden of Disease (GBD)

disclaimer: Age-standardised prevalence, all ages, of moderate or worse hearing loss (>=35 dB in the better ear). South and Central Asia dominate due to childhood otitis media and noise exposure.
trivia: Nepal's rates are driven by chronic ear infections combined with limited paediatric ENT access; national screening programmes started only in 2018.

title: Highest visual impairment prevalence
prompt: Name the countries with the highest age-standardised prevalence of moderate-to-severe visual impairment or blindness.

source.name: IAPB Vision Atlas / IHME GBD

disclaimer: Age-standardised prevalence of moderate-to-severe vision impairment plus blindness, all ages. Cataract backlog and refractive-error under-correction are the biggest drivers.
trivia: The largest gaps between actual and 'preventable' blindness cluster in South Asia and the Sahel — over 80% of cases are treatable if surgical capacity existed.

title: Highest per-capita medicine spending
prompt: Name the countries with the highest per-capita retail spending on prescription and non-prescription pharmaceuticals.

source.name: OECD Health Statistics — Pharmaceutical Expenditure

disclaimer: Retail pharmaceutical spending per capita in USD PPP; excludes hospital-administered drugs. OECD countries only.
trivia: US per-capita drug spending is roughly double the OECD average — driven by list prices for branded biologics, not volume of medicines consumed.

title: Largest pharmaceutical R&D spending
prompt: Name the countries whose pharmaceutical industry spends the most on research and development.

source.name: EFPIA — The Pharmaceutical Industry in Figures

disclaimer: Total pharma industry R&D expenditure (public + private) by country of R&D activity, in billion USD. Reflects where R&D happens, not headquarters location.
trivia: Roughly half of global pharma R&D happens in the US alone; Switzerland punches far above its size thanks to Roche and Novartis's Basel cluster.

title: Highest anxiety and depression prevalence
prompt: Name the countries with the highest age-standardised prevalence of anxiety and depressive disorders combined.

source.name: IHME — Global Burden of Disease (GBD)

disclaimer: Age-standardised prevalence of any anxiety or depressive disorder, all ages. Conflict, displacement, and better mental health screening all push rates up.
trivia: Portugal's rate is one of the highest in Europe — driven by long-diagnosed depression and heavy benzodiazepine prescribing dating to the 1990s.

title: Most public spending on prevention
prompt: Name the countries whose governments spend the largest share of health budgets on preventive care.

source.name: OECD Health at a Glance — Preventive Care Expenditure

disclaimer: Preventive care as a percentage of total current health expenditure (SHA definition — screening, immunisation, health promotion, epidemiological surveillance). OECD countries only.
trivia: Italy's high share reflects sustained investment in a national vaccination programme and screening after the COVID-era public health reset.

title: Highest daily newspaper circulation
prompt: Name the countries with the highest total daily newspaper circulation (paid print copies per day, all titles combined).

source.name: WAN-IFRA — World Press Trends Report

disclaimer: Combined paid daily print circulation across all national and regional titles. Excludes digital-only and free (metro) papers unless the industry association reports them as paid.
trivia: Japan has historically led per-capita newspaper reading, with Yomiuri Shimbun long holding the Guinness record as the world's largest-circulation daily paper.

title: Most radio broadcasting stations
prompt: Name the countries with the most operating radio broadcasting stations (AM, FM and shortwave combined).

source.name: CIA World Factbook — Communications: Broadcast Media

disclaimer: Counts licensed terrestrial broadcast stations across AM, FM, and shortwave bands. Community, commercial and public stations all included; internet-only radio is excluded.
trivia: The United States alone has more licensed FM stations than the next several countries combined, largely because the FCC licenses each low-power FM translator as its own station.

title: Most books published per year
prompt: Name the countries publishing the most new book titles per year (new and revised editions across all subjects).

source.name: UNESCO Institute for Statistics / International Publishers Association

disclaimer: New and revised titles published in the year, per national publishing association reporting. Excludes self-published titles unless included in the country's ISBN authority totals.
trivia: China has led global new-title output since 2011 and publishes more new titles annually than the entire European Union combined.

title: Most TV channels in operation
prompt: Name the countries with the most terrestrial, cable and satellite TV channels licensed for domestic distribution.

source.name: European Audiovisual Observatory / national regulators (FCC, Ofcom, KCC, SARFT)

disclaimer: Includes free-to-air, pay-TV and dedicated satellite channels licensed for the domestic market. Streaming-only services are not counted.
trivia: The United States and China each license more TV channels than the entire African continent combined; Russia's high count is inflated by many regional variants of federal networks.

title: Most magazine titles published
prompt: Name the countries with the most consumer and trade magazine titles in active publication.

source.name: FIPP — World Magazine Media Congress data / national publisher associations

disclaimer: Count of registered active magazine titles (consumer + B2B/trade) as reported by the national magazine publishers' association. Digital-only titles included where the national body registers them.
trivia: Germany's magazine market is dominated by a handful of publishing houses (Bauer, Burda, Gruner+Jahr) that each individually publish hundreds of titles across Europe.

title: Largest podcast markets by revenue
prompt: Name the countries with the largest podcast advertising and subscription revenue markets.

source.name: IAB / PwC Global Entertainment & Media Outlook — Podcast segment

disclaimer: Total podcast advertising plus paid subscription revenue in USD. Numbers are lightly rounded and rest on IAB/PwC market estimates rather than reported company revenue.
trivia: The US podcast advertising market alone is larger than every other country's total podcast market combined, driven by Joe Rogan, Wondery, and iHeart's ad-supported catalog.

title: Most annual film festivals hosted
prompt: Name the countries hosting the most annual film festivals (feature-film, documentary and short-film festivals combined).

source.name: FIAPF — International Federation of Film Producers Associations / FilmFreeway registry

disclaimer: Counts recurring annual film festivals registered with FIAPF or listed on FilmFreeway as active. One-off events and student-only campus festivals are excluded.
trivia: The United States hosts more film festivals than any other country, but France's Cannes remains the single most valuable acquisition market, generating over $1B in film deals annually.

title: Most cinema screens per capita
prompt: Name the countries with the most cinema screens per capita (screens per 100,000 residents).

source.name: MPA Theme Report / UNESCO Institute for Statistics — Feature Films and Cinema data

disclaimer: Number of commercial cinema screens per 100,000 residents. Countries with fewer than 50 total screens are excluded to avoid microstate distortions.
trivia: Iceland tops the per-capita list despite having under 50 total screens; France's high figure reflects its unique regulatory environment which subsidizes small-town independent cinemas.

title: Largest print advertising markets
prompt: Name the countries with the largest print advertising markets (newspaper + magazine ad spend combined).

source.name: GroupM / Zenith / Dentsu — Global Ad Spend Forecast: Print segment

disclaimer: Combined newspaper and magazine ad revenue in USD. Digital editions of print titles are excluded and counted under digital display instead.
trivia: Japan and Germany remain unusually strong print ad markets in the digital era: both have highly loyal newspaper subscription bases and premium-brand luxury magazine spending that has resisted the global collapse.

title: Highest press freedom score
prompt: Name the countries with the highest press freedom scores (i.e. freest media environments).

source.name: Reporters Without Borders — World Press Freedom Index

disclaimer: Rank 1 corresponds to the country with the freest press environment in the RSF composite score. The index combines political, economic, legal, social and safety indicators; microstate results (San Marino, Liechtenstein) are excluded where the sample size is too small.
trivia: The Nordic countries have swept the top of the RSF ranking almost every year since the index launched in 2002, with Norway holding the #1 slot for eight consecutive years.
